SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No.
Special branch xxxxxxxx
REPORT
Date January 21, 19 38.
Subject Release of Oo Ching-wen upon furnishing guarantee bond.
Made by and Forwarded by C.D.I. Ross

In accordance with the instructions of the D.C.(Special Branch), the prisoner named Oo Ching-wen (錦文), who was arrested in Room 218, Bubbling Well Apartments, Bubbling Well Road, on December 30, 1937, together with several others in connection with national salvation activities, was released on the afternoon of January 21. A guarantee bond to ensure future good conduct of the accused, which is signed by his father, named Oo Ah-tu (鄔阿兔), an employee of the Yoh Lai Lodging House, Lane 591, 178 Bubbling Well Road, and witnessed by Yih Sing-zeui (葉星壽), uncle of the accused, an employee of the Tsai Dong Tuh Medicine Shop, 455 Honan Road, and Yang Yuin-sung (楊雲生), proprietor of the Yuin Sung Store, 1017 Sinza Road, was obtained and is attached herewith.

D.C.(Special Branch)

(印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE * 21 JAN 1938 *)

C. D. I.

由特别处首席侦探员 Ross 制作并转呈

遵照特别处副总巡的指示，因涉嫌救国活动于1937年12月30日在静安寺路 Bubbling Well Apartments（原文不清，音译：巴布林威尔公寓）218室与其他数人一同被捕的囚犯 Oo Ching-wen（鄔錦文），已于1月21日下午获释。为确保被告日后行为端正，已取得由其父 Oo Ah-tu（鄔阿兔）签署的保释具结书，其父系静安寺路178号591弄 Yoh Lai Lodging House（原文不清，音译：约来旅馆）职员；并由被告叔父 Yih Sing-zeui（葉星壽，河南路455号 Tsai Dong Tuh Medicine Shop（原文不清，音译：蔡东土药店）职员）及 Yang Yuin-sung（楊雲生，新闸路1017号 Yuin Sung Store（原文不清，音译：云生商店）店主）见证。该具结书附后。

特别处副总巡

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 * 1938年1月21日 *）

首席侦探员

Subject (in full) Release of King Jing (金瑾) and Xing Sung-dien(邢舜田)
                  upon furnishing guarantee bonds.
Made by         and             Forwarded by C.D.I. D.B. Ross

    In accordance with the instructions of the D.C.
(Special Branch), the two prisoners named King Jing and
Ying Sung-dien, who were arrested on December 30, 1937
and January 2, 1938, together with a number of others in
connection with national salvation activities, were
released on the afternoon of January 19 upon guarantee
bonds (attached) for future good conduct being furnished.
The guarantors and witnesses for the two accused are
Messrs. Wang Mang-tseu(汪孟邹 ) and Zung Tseng-tsai(程正齋)
who were recommended by Mr. H. C. Chen, Chinese Educational
Officer of the Shanghai Municipal Council, and Mr. Zung
Hai-foong (程海峯 ), Chief of the China Branch of the
International Labour Bureau.

                                        C. D. I.

D.C. (Special Branch)

曾于1930年4月18日因持有煽动性文献及阴谋颠覆中华民国宪法而被捕。
他被命令移交给公安局。
1月14日上午，收到一封来自杨守仁（Yang Sheu Zung）的信（附后），他希望为上述名单第4号的被告之一王乙（Wong Yih）提供担保。
特别处副总巡的指示和建议已传达给“A”区警司、成都路负责督察及高级侦探，结果是正在向刑事处副总巡申请移送剩余在押人员。
鉴于所涉及的困难，建议将所有被告送往同一目的地，乘坐同一艘船只。
附后的是四名获释人员的担保表格，以及在青岛路77号查获物品的清单。

REPORT
Subject Arrest of a male Chinese at 77 Tsingtao Road.
Made by D.S. Lockwood Forwarded by C Crawford D.I.

At 2 p.m. January 7, 1938, detectives on observation duty at 77 Tsingtao Road arrested a male Chinese named Wong Foo Pau (汪府宝), a student of the Kuo Kwang Middle School, Avenue Road near Carter Road, residing at flat No.50 Paris Court Avenue Dubail. Wong stated that he had a friend named Tsang Yung-ling (張文霖) who left the Kuo Kwang Middle School about one month ago. After he left, he sent Wong a letter c/o the school saying that if he needed books to read he should call at 77 Tsingtao Road and ask for him. A few days ago, Wong noticed that the film "The Good Earth" was showing at the Nanking Theatre and knowing Tsang had the book when he was at school, Wong thought that he would borrow it. It was with that intention that he went to No.77 Tsingtao Road. When he arrived there he was arrested. Wong states that he does not belong to any political organizations and also states that this was the first occasion on which he had visited 77 Tsingtao Road. The truth of this statement is partly borne out by the fact that the female in custody named Ho Ping alias Ho Ying, whose statements in regard to the other accused have been found to be reliable, when confronted with Wong stated that she did not recognize him and had not seen him before at 77 Tsingtao Road.

Acting in cooperation with detectives attached to the French Police Political Department, D.S. Lockwood and D.S.I. Liu visited Apartment 50, Paris Court, Avenue Dubail, and verified Wong Foo Pau's statement to the

事由：在青岛路77号逮捕一名中国男子。
制作人 D.S. Lockwood 转呈人 C Crawford 侦探督察

1938年1月7日下午2时，在青岛路77号执行监视任务的侦探逮捕了一名中国男子，名为汪府宝（Wong Foo Pau），系爱文义路近卡特路国华中学学生，居住在杜拜尔路巴黎公寓50号单元。汪称他有一位朋友名叫张文霖（Tsang Yung-ling），约一个月前离开国华中学。离开后，他通过学校转交了一封信给汪，说如果需要读书，可以去青岛路77号找他。几天前，汪注意到南京大戏院正在放映电影《大地》，知道张在学校时有这本书，汪便想借来看。正是出于这个目的，他去了青岛路77号。当他到达那里时被捕。汪声称他不属于任何政治组织，并称这是他第一次访问青岛路77号。这一说法的部分真实性得到了在押女子何平（别名何英）的证实，该女子关于其他被告的陈述已被发现是可靠的，当与汪对质时，她表示不认识他，以前在青岛路77号也未见过他。

在与法国警察政治部附属侦探的合作下，D.S. Lockwood 和副督察长 Liu 走访了杜拜尔路巴黎公寓50室，核实了汪府宝的陈述

根据分区督察（特别股）的指示，12月31日下午3时，成都路分局侦探长 Dickson、华人侦探探员 Sih Tse-liang 以及侦探长 McKeown 前往静安寺路旁东义里的海关职员俱乐部，试图寻找一名名为 Zung Tsing（□ □）的人，此人被被告徐振佑提及为职业界救国会成员。Zung Tsing 系该俱乐部雇员，警方造访时不在场内，据称其居住在伯基尔路（Burkill Road）的一处房屋内，门牌号不详。特别股侦探正在进行查询，以期找到此人。

12月31日下午5时30分，老闸分局副侦探长 Black、华人侦探探员 Sih Tse-liang 以及侦探长 McKeown 前往云南路35号的仁济堂善会。办公室经过搜查，但未获结果。在接受问询时，职员们表示他们无意参与救国运动，并决定将发送给他们的所有宣传材料移交警方。

已进行查询，以查明位于爱多亚路与河南路转角浦东银行32室设有办事处的外商企业联益社的任何成员是否为当前运动的发起者，但未能获得直接证据。根据指示，中央分局侦探长 Francis、侦探长 McKeown 以及第45号华人侦探警士于1月4日上午前往该办事处

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No.
S.1. Special Branch
REPORT
Date January 4, 1938.
Subject National Salvation Movements - further arrests.
Made by D.S. Larby Forwarded by

Between 1 p.m. and 3 p.m. January 3, 1938, the two individuals mentioned hereunder were arrested by detectives attached to Chengtu Road Station who were posted at 77 Tsingtao Road:-
(1) Wong Moo Vung(王慕文), alias Wong Chi(王起).
(2) Ting Vung Sung(丁文深).
The first accused states that he is a teacher and that until August, 1937, he had been employed at the Soo Soo Primary School(蘇蘇小學), 265, Zang An Lee, Rue Kraetzer, of which his sister, Wong Woo(王和) is the principal. Subsequent to the outbreak of hostilities in the Shanghai area, Wong joined the Refugee Section of the Shanghai Vocational Circles National Salvation Association, Lane 132, House 4, Park Road, a committee member of which - Pan Yang Yao - is a friend of his. Wong states, however, that he does not know where Pan at present can be located.
After the closure of the Shanghai Vocational Circles National Salvation Association by the Municipal Police about a month ago, Wong in conjunction with a number of ex-staff members of the Refugee Section of the aforementioned association, together with certain of the supervisors of the various local refugee camps formed the "Staff Members' Lien Nyi (Mutual Aid) Society of Various Refugee Camps," the offices of which were located at Room 218, Bubbling Well Building, Bubbling Well Road. Wong was appointed Secretary of this Society, the ostensible object of which was to promote education among the refugees, and was assisted by the following individuals:-
Wong Min Yang(王名揚)

（批：See report dets 29.1.37 S.1.）

1938年1月3日下午1时至3时之间，下述两人被驻守于青岛路77号的成都路分局侦探逮捕：-
(1) Wong Moo Vung(王慕文)，又名 Wong Chi(王起)。
(2) Ting Vung Sung(丁文深)。
第一被告称其为教师，直至1937年8月，受雇于克雷泽尔路（Rue Kraetzer）脏安里265号苏苏小学，该校校长为其姐姐王和。上海地区战事爆发后，王加入上海职业界救国会难民部（公园路4号132弄），该会委员潘仰尧是其朋友。王称，但他不知道潘目前身在何处。
在上海职业界救国会约一个月前被市警察关闭后，王与该会难民部的前工作人员以及当地各难民收容所的某些管理员共同组建了“各难民收容所工作人员联益社”，社址位于静安寺路静安大楼218室。王被任命为该社秘书，该社表面宗旨为促进难民教育，并由以下人士协助：-
王名扬

（批注：见1937年1月29日 S.1. 侦探报告。）

According to Wong the Society is divided into three sections, namely Educational, Employment and Social Sections, the names of the responsible members of which are unknown to him. In view of the position held by the accused, the truth of the latter statement is open to doubt.

During the questioning, Wong made particular reference to Mr. H.C. Chen( 陈鶴琴 ), Chinese Education Officer of the Municipal Council, who, he stated, had expressed his approval of the aims of this Society.

Subjected to further questioning, the accused admitted that while he was unaware of the persons responsible for the placing of the propaganda matter in the Room 218, Bubbling Well Building, he had, together with a friend, one Woo Chuen( 吴塋 ), visited the Ching Sing( 鏡星 ) Printing Shop at 224 Sinza Road and on the instructions of Wong Min-yang who is already in custody ordered the printing of 20,000 paper national flags and 20,000 paper slips to be inscribed with slogans of a national salvation nature. A number of these flags and slips were subsequently delivered to the Society's office.

On learning of the raids carried out by the Municipal Police on the Society's premises, Wong revisited the Ching Sing Printing Shop and warned the shopmaster to destroy

The third accused, Sung Kao, admits that he was

Translation of a circular delivered to 77 Tsingtao Road
by Sung Kau (arrested) on the forenoon of Jan. 1, 1938
------------

Dear Comrade:

1938 - the first New Year since the beginning
of the war of resistance - will soon be here. In orderto
celebrate this auspicious occasion, and in order to
discuss our future plans, we will hold a members' New
Year gala meeting at 2 p.m. January 1, 1938, in the Zung
In English Language School, corner of Ningpo and Shanse Roads.
The second year members' general meeting will be held at the
same time. During the meeting, a report will be submitted
on the record of work done in the past. A new executive
committee will be elected. This will be followed by a
concert.

You are requested to attend and bring with
you as many new comrades as possible.

Victory for the New Language Movement!

The Shanghai New Language
Research Institute.

31.12.37.

------

Brief Rules for the Junior Esperanto Class

Name: Junior Esperanto Class.

Object: The learning of Esperanto.

Tuition hours: 4.30 to 6 p.m. every day except Saturdays
and Sundays.

Term of study: Two months.

Commencement of class: Monday, January 6.

Place: In the Central District of the International
Settlement. Exact address will be announced
later.

Place of enrollment: Post Office Box 1741.

The Education Department of the Shanghai
New Language Research Society.

亲爱的同志：

1938年——抗战开始后的第一个新年——即将来临。为了庆祝这一吉祥时刻，并讨论我们未来的计划，我们将于1938年1月1日下午2时，在宁波路与山西路交界处的中英学校（Zung In English Language School，音译）举行会员新年联欢大会。第二届会员大会将同时举行。会议期间，将提交过去的工作记录报告。将选举新的执行委员会。随后将举行音乐会。

请阁下出席，并尽可能携带新同志参加。

新语言运动胜利！

上海新语研究所。

1937年12月31日。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

The following is the statement of Woo ying ( 吴 英 ) ,
native of Kiangsu ( Sungkiang) taken by me D.S. Lockwood
at Chengtu Rd.Stn.on the 1.1.38 and interpreted by Clerk Wong Chia-teing

My name is Woo ying, age 23, native of Sunkiung,
Kiangsu Province, residing in King Jui Primary School
( 金 瑞 小 学 ), Route Ghisi, where I am employed as a
teacher in the Mandarin dialect.

I proceeded to 77 Tsingtao Road in order to deliver
a letter to one named Jong ( □ ), who is the editor of a
magazine entitled "Chinese Youth" ( 中 國 少 年 ). This
magazine is published in 77 Tsingtao Road. A friend named
Jong Mang Woo ( □ □ □ ) residing in Sian sent me a letter
with the enclosure and requested me to deliver it.

This is my first visit to 77 Tsingtao Road since the
commencement of hostilities. Prior to the summer however,
I visited this address frequently in order to deliver
articles for the "Chinese Youth" periodical which had been
submitted by my friend, who resides in Sian.

I have never participated in any political organizations
nor have I undertaken any national salvation activities. I
know nothing of the activities of Ling or Tsu.

Signed: 吴 英

以下是吴英（Woo ying）的陈述，江苏（松江）人，由我 D.S. Lockwood 于1938年1月1日在成都路警署录取，并由文员 Wong Chia-teing 翻译

我叫吴英，23岁，江苏省松江人，居住在格希路（Route Ghisi，音译）金瑞小学（King Jui Primary School），我在该校担任国语教师。

我前往青岛路77号是为了向一位姓钟（Jong，原文不清）的人递交一封信，他是名为《中国少年》杂志的编辑。该杂志在青岛路77号出版。一位名叫钟孟武（Jong Mang Woo，原文不清）的朋友居住在西安，他寄给我一封信及附件，并请我代为递交。

这是自战事爆发以来我第一次访问青岛路77号。然而在夏季之前，我经常访问该地址，以便递交由我居住在西安的朋友提交的《中国少年》期刊稿件。

我从未参与任何政治组织，也未从事任何救国活动。我对凌或朱的活动一无所知。

签名：吴英

The following is the statement of Woo Zung Hsiung ( 吳 仁 勇 )
native of Soochow taken by me D.S. Lockwood
at Chengtu Rd. Stn. on the 1.1.38 and interpreted by Clerk Wong Chia-tsing.

My name is Woo Zung Hsiung, age 22, native of Soochow,
single, unemployed, residing in No. 7 Pah Luh Li ( 柏 陸 里 ),
Yates Road. I was formerly employed as a godown keeper in
the Kia Fong Cotton Mill ( 嘉 豐 紗 廠 ), Kiating, Kiangsu,
which closed following the declaration of hostilities.
At 10 a.m. January 1, 1938, I proceeded to 77 Tsingtao
Road with a view to interviewing a man named Loo Vung Nan
( 盧 雲 南 ) who promised to obtain employment for me in
a refugee camp.
I am not a member of any society. On December 1st I
applied for membership to a group known as the Popular
Education Society, 77 Tsingtao Road. To date I have
received no reply to my application. I made this application
in order to facilitate my search for employment. I am not
connected with any anti-Japanese organization nor have I
taken part in the distribution of propaganda matter.

Signed: 吳仁勇

我叫吴仁勇，22岁，苏州人，未婚，失业，居住在叶特路（Yates Road，音译）柏陆里7号。我以前在江苏嘉定嘉丰纱厂（Kia Fong Cotton Mill）担任仓库管理员，该厂在宣战后关闭。
1938年1月1日上午10时，我前往青岛路77号，意在会见一位名叫卢云南（Loo Vung Nan）的人，他答应为我在难民营安排工作。
我不是任何社团的成员。12月1日，我申请加入一个名为“大众教育社”的团体，地址在青岛路77号。至今我未收到对我申请的回复。我提出此申请是为了便于寻找工作。我与任何反日组织无关，也未参与分发宣传品。

签名：吴仁勇

我叫沈鵠，18岁，浙江嘉兴人，未婚，学生，与父母同住布勃雷路（Bubulay Road，音译）104号。我以前是大西路光华中学的学生。

At 3 p.m. December 30, a party of Police from
Chengtu Road under D.I. Hill, D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken and
D.S. McKeown, acting upon the instructions of the
D.C. (Special Branch) visited room 218, 749 Bubbling
Well Road, suspected of being a depot of the national
salvation association. A large quantity of Chinese
flags, anti-Japanese greeting cards, national salvation
propaganda, and a mimeograph machine were seized. The
seizure was removed to the Special Branch and is at
present in process of classification. Present in the
office at the time of the Police visit were three male
Chinese namely :
(1) Wong Ming Yang (王明揚), salesman for the
China National Insurance Company;
(2) Yang Yuan Kong (楊元康), shroff in the employ
of the Foch Rubber Company, 490 Avenue Foch;
(3) Tseu Zung Teh (周成德), unemployed.
These three persons were taken to Chengtu Road Station and
full statements were obtained (copies attached).
The 1st accused Wong Ming Yang, was definitely
connected with the National Salvation Movement. He admits
being formerly a member of the Foreign Owned Firms Chinese
Employees Lien Nyi Society which formed part of the
Vocational Circles National Salvation Association which
was dissolved following the withdrawal of Chinese troops
from Shanghai. He agreed to participate in the revival
of the National Salvation Movement at the request of one

12月30日下午3时，由成都路巡捕房督察长（D.I.）Hill、副督察长（D.S.I.）高延根（Kao Yen-ken）及副探长（D.S.）McKeown率领的一队警员，遵照特别课副总监（D.C.）的指示，前往静安寺路749号218室进行搜查，该处被怀疑为救国协会的据点。现场查获大量中国国旗、抗日贺年卡、救国宣传品以及一台油印机。所获物品已移送至特别课，目前正在进行分类整理。警方到达时，办公室内有三名华籍男子在场，即：
(1) 王明揚 (Wong Ming Yang)，中国保险公司推销员；
(2) 楊元康 (Yang Yuan Kong)，福煦路490号福煦橡胶公司出纳员；
(3) 周成德 (Tseu Zung Teh)，无业。
上述三人被带往成都路巡捕房，并取得了完整供词（副本附后）。
第一被告王明揚与救国运动确有牵连。他承认曾是外商华员联益社成员，该社隶属于职业界救国会，后者在中国军队撤出上海后被解散。他应蒙脱班路（Rue Montauban）法亚保险公司买办楊延脩（Yang Yien Siu）之请，同意参与救国运动的复兴工作。

（批：X ben D/651）

Yang Yien Siu (楊延脩), comprador of the Assurance

social standing, appears to be a leading light in the
present movement. His residential address is not known.
Wong Ming Yang admitted that he was engaged in delivering
articles including flags and anti-Japanese greeting cards
on behalf of the National Salvation Association.

The second accused Yang Yuan Kong admits having been
a member of the Vocational Circles National Salvation
Association prior to the withdrawal of Chinese troops,
and states that he was requested on December 30 to take
an active part in the movement. His statement that he
has taken no part in the movement is belied by the fact
that he was in the office at the time of the Police visit.

The third accused Tseu Zung Teh states that a
friend found employment for him in the office at room 218,
distributing cotton vests at a monthly wage of $6.00.
Later he states that a person in the office told him to
distribute 300 greeting cards and 3,000 Chinese National
Flags to all who applied for them. Although Tseu denies
all knowledge of the organization, he is of average
intelligence and doubtless realized the importance of the
work in which he was engaged.

Consequent upon detectives being left to maintain a
watch over the premises, eight male Chinese were arrested
between 6 p.m. and 12 midnight, December 30, namely :

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of WONG MING YANG (王明揚)
native of Ningpo ........................................taken by me D.S. McKeown
at Chen-tu Rd. Stn on the 30/12/37 ....................and interpreted by D.S.I. Kao Yen Ken

My name is Wong Ming Yang, aged 24, a native of Ningpo,
and married. I am a salesman of the China National Insurance
Company, China Land Bank Building, corner of Peking and Kiang-
se Roads, and reside at 20 Kiu Foh Li, Malalay Road. I am
a member of the Foreign Owned Firms Chinese Employees Lien
Yi Society, formerly situated at 115 Hankow Road and now at
Footung Bank Building (2nd floor), corner of Avenue Ed. VII
and Honan Road, which was part of the Vocational Circles
National Salvation Association. Automatically I became
member of the national salvation association, which was dis-
solved following the withdrawal of the Chinese forces.
At the end of November 1937, Yang Yien Siu (楊延修),
compradore of the Assurance Franco-Asiatique, Rue Montauban,
and concurrently a staff member of the Organization Section
of the Foreign Owned Firm Chinese Employees' Lien Yi Society,
asked me to assist him in conducting national salvation works
among refugees. He belongs to the vocational Circles National
Salvation Association, with secret offices the addresses of
which I do not know. Although I am a member of this organiza-
tion, I merely receive orders from Yang. The work among the
the refugees is a part of the programme of the Vocational
Circles National Salvation Association. My principal work is
to deliver articles, including flags and cards. Although a
number of persons work in this organization, I only know the
following persons:-
1. Yang Yien Siu
2. Yang Yuan Kong (in custody).

以下为王明揚（WONG MING YANG），宁波籍人士........................................的供词，由本人 D.S. McKeown
于1937年12月30日在成都路捕房 ....................................录取，并由 D.S.I. Kao Yen Ken 翻译

我叫王明揚，24岁，宁波人，已婚。我是中国保险公司的推销员，公司地址位于北京路与江西路转角的中国银行大楼，居住在马拉莱路（Malalay Road）久福里20号。我是外商华员联益社的成员，该社原址位于汉口路115号，现址位于爱多亚路（Avenue Ed. VII）与河南路转角的福通银行大楼（二楼），该社是职业界救国会的一部分。我自动成为救国会会员，该会在华军撤退后解散。
1937年11月底，蒙脱班路（Rue Montauban）法亚保险公司（Assurance Franco-Asiatique）买办、兼外商华员联益社组织科职员的杨延修（Yang Yien Siu），请我协助他在难民中开展救国工作。他属于职业界救国会，其秘密办公地点的地址我并不知道。虽然我是该组织的成员，但我仅接受杨的命令。难民工作只是职业界救国会计划的一部分。我的主要工作是递送物品，包括旗帜和卡片。虽然有许多人在该组织工作，但我只认识以下人员：-
1. 杨延修
2. 杨元孔（Yang Yuan Kong，在押）。

3. Wong Moo Vung (王慕文), unemployed, living in Room 218,
Bubbling Well Building, Bubbling Well Road, who deals
with the printing of the cards and other matters.

4. Chun Hung (龚虹), a school teacher by profession, where-
abouts unknown.

I understand that all the other work is detailed to persons
by Yang Lien Jiu. Room 218 was formerly occupied by the
Native Bank Employees Lien Iyi Society and vacated about three
days ago. From the commencement of December up to now, I and
the other members used the room as a communication address.
Through the arrangements made by Wong Moo Vung, a quantity of
flags, cards, printed matter as well as a mimeograph were
brought to the room about two or three days ago.

With regard to the "Refugee Camp Workers Lien Iyi Society,
I understand that before the withdrawal of Chinese troops
from Shanghai, the Vocational Circles National Salvation Asso-
ciation convened meetings of a number of workers of refugee
camps from time to time, and thus they formed an organization
known as the "Refugee Camp Workers Lien Iyi Society". I
also know that Chun Hung is the member of the Vocational
Circles National Salvation Association who communicates with
the Refugee Camp Workers Lien Iyi Society.

At about 2.30 p.m. December 30, I arrived at the room
in the Bubbling Building, Bubbling Well Road, with a view
to discussing with Wong Moo Vung the distribution of the flags
cards and a periodical entitled "Friends of Refugees" to
various refugee camps before the New Year. While I was waiting

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Yang Yuan Kong (楊元康)
native of Ningpo taken by me D. J. McEwan
at Chengtu Rd. Stn on the 30/12/37 and interpreted by D. J. I. Kao Yen Ken

My name is Yang Yuan Kong, aged 24, native of Ningpo,
and a staff in the employ of the Foch Rubber Co., 490 Av.
Foch. I reside on the premises of the firm.

At about 10 a.m. December 30, at the corner of Bubbling
Well and Yates Roads, I met Wong Ming Yang (王明揚), now in
custody, a salesman in the employ of the China Insurance Co.,
Avenue Joffre (formerly situated on Szechuen Road), who was
a fellow member of the Vocational Circles National Salvation
Association prior to the withdrawal of Chinese troops from
Shanghai. He told me that as the situation was very tense,
workers for the national salvation movement were few and that
it was proposed that national flags should be hoisted in
refugee camps in celebration of the New Year Festival. He did
not tell me who proposed the movement. He requested me to
call at his "place", Room 218 Bubbling Well Building, Bubbling
Well Road, off Carter Road, at 2 p.m. and take a bundle of
national flags to the Jen Chi Tang Benevolent Society, 35
Yunnan Road, which takes charge of a part of local refugee
camps. At 2.30 p.m. I arrived at the room where I met Wong
and was given a bundle of flags with instructions to take it
to the Refugee Reception Section of the Jen Chi Tang (i.e.
the Disaster Relief Federation of Shanghai Benevolent Societies)

I have not engaged in any "national salvation" activities
since the withdrawal of the Chinese troops, when all local
national salvation associations were dissolved. I learned
recently from my friends that these associations had lately
endeavoured to resume operations secretly and were maintaining

本人名叫杨元康，现年 24 岁，籍贯宁波，系福煦路 490 号福昌橡胶公司（Foch Rubber Co.）职员。本人居住在公司宿舍内。

12 月 30 日上午 10 时许，本人在静安寺路与 Yates 路（今黄陂北路）转角处遇见王明揚（王明揚），此人目前在押，系前位于四川路、现位于霞飞路的中国保险公司推销员。在中国军队撤离上海之前，他曾是职业界救国会会员。他告诉本人，鉴于局势非常紧张，从事救国运动的工作人员寥寥无几，有人提议在难民收容所悬挂国旗以庆祝新年。他并未告知本人是谁提出了这一倡议。他请本人于下午 2 时前往其“地点”，即卡德路旁静安寺路静安大楼 218 室，领取一捆国旗并送至云南路 35 号仁济堂善会，该机构负责管理部分本地难民收容所。下午 2 时 30 分，本人到达该房间，见到王明揚，并收到一捆国旗，奉命将其送往仁济堂难民接待处（即上海慈善团体联合救灾会）。

自中国军队撤离、本地各救国会解散以来，本人未参与任何“救国”活动。本人近期从朋友处获悉，这些协会最近试图秘密恢复运作，并维持着

The following is the statement of Tseu Zung reh (周成德)
native of Ningpo taken by me D. J. McKeown
at Chengtu Rd Stn on the 30/12/37 and interpreted by Clerk Loh Tei Kong

My name is Tseu Zung Teh, age 18, native of
Ningpo, single and unemployed.
Following the outbreak of the local Sino-Japanese
hostilities, I left for Ningpo and remained at my native
place until December 4 when I returned here by steamer,
with a view to seeking employment. After returning, I
stayed in the premises of the Kuh Sung Company, a cotton
exchange agency, No.1 Szechuen Road, now closed, where I
was formerly employed as a telephone operator. (It was a
Chinese concern, but the manager was Japanese). Four days
later I left this place and went to reside with my friend
Woo Dah-ming (鄔達明), room 15, 110 Avenue Edward VII.
Woo formerly was also employed by the Kuh Sung Company
as an accountant.
During the afternoon of December 12, at about
2 p.m., I went to see Zee Tseng-yue (徐振裕), a friend
of mine, and an apprentice of the Van Foong (萬丰)
Cereal Hong, No.1 Szechuen Road, at his place of employment,
and requested him to seek employment for me. He promised
to consider my request. On the forenoon of December 13,
Zee Tseng-yue came to see me at Room 15, 110 Avenue Edward
VII, and told me to see one named Zung (程), at 10 Doong
Yih Li, Bubbling Well Road. I accordingly went there on
the afternoon of the same day, when Zung asked me to take
care of old cotton clothes contributed by the public for
the relief of refugees, and promised me a monthly subsidy
of $6.00. I went to Room 218, Bubbling Well Apartments

以下为周成德（Tseu Zung reh [原文拼写错误，应为 Teh]）之供词，籍贯宁波，由本人 D. J. McKeown 于 1937 年 12 月 30 日在成都路捕房录取，并由书记员 Loh Tei Kong 担任翻译。

本人名叫周成德（Tseu Zung Teh），现年 18 岁，籍贯宁波，未婚，失业。

本地中日敌对行动爆发后，本人前往宁波，并在家乡停留至 12 月 4 日，随后乘轮船返回此地，旨在寻找工作。回来后，本人住在四川路 1 号库松公司（Kuh Sung Company，一家棉花交易所代理机构，现已关闭）的 premises 内，本人此前受雇于该公司担任电话接线员。（这是一家华商企业，但经理是日本人）。四天后，本人离开该处，前往朋友鄔達明（Woo Dah-ming）处居住，地址为爱多亚路 110 号 15 室。鄔達明此前也受雇于库松公司担任会计。

12 月 12 日下午约 2 时，本人去工作地点看望朋友徐振裕（Zee Tseng-yue），他是四川路 1 号萬丰（Van Foong）粮行学徒，并请他帮本人找工作。他答应考虑本人的请求。12 月 13 日上午，徐振裕来到爱多亚路 110 号 15 室看望本人，并让本人去静安寺路东义里 10 号见一位姓程（Zung）的人。本人遂于当天下午前往，程某要求本人负责保管公众捐赠用于救济难民的旧棉衣，并承诺每月给予本人 6.00 元津贴。本人奉程某之命，于

and instructed me to distribute them to all persons who

Before December 15, I was living with Woo Dah-ming
in Room 15, 110 Avenue Edward VII, and Zee Tseng-yue, who
had resigned from the Van Foong Cereal Hong, also came to
stay with us on December 14. Due to the fact that Woo
Dah-ming objected to us living in his room, Zee Tseng-yue
and I removed to the room above the Keng Sing Li (耕莘里),

removed to Room 218, Bubbling Well Apartments, Bubbling Well

this address during the afternoon of the same day. Zee,
however, came to occupy the room on December 28.
On December 28, Wong Mou-wen showed me some 3,000
copies of the Chinese National Flag printed on paper, and
300 new year greeting cards kept in the room, and told me
to distribute them to all persons who called at the room
and applied for them. On the forenoon of December 29,
three Chinese (all about thirty years of age), claiming
to be members of refugee camps, came to the room, and each

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Lee Tseng Yue (李增裕)
native of Ningpo taken by me D.J. McKeown
at Chen tu Rd. Stn. on the 30/12/37 and interpreted by Clerk Liao Chung Chien

My name is Zee Tseng Yue, aged 21, native of Ningpo, single.
I am unemployed, formerly working as a clerk in the Van Foong
(萬豐) Cereal Co., 120 Avenue Edward VII, and leaving the
employment on December 14, 1937 owing to trade depression.
I reside in Room 218, Bubbling Well Apartments, Bubbling Well
Road to which address I removed on December 27.
I joined the Vocational Circles National Salvation
Association in August 1937 when it was situated in the Sing
Kwan Primary School, Chungking Road. I was also a member of
the Cereal Co. Employees Lien Nyi Club, Min Kuo Road, which was
dissolved after the withdrawal of the Chinese forces from
Shanghai.
Although I was a member of the Vocational Circles National
Salvation Association I did not take part in its activities
except soliciting funds from friends and relatives on its
behalf on two occasions in September and October, 1937, respect-
ively.
My friend Tseu Zung Teh (周成德) was formerly employed
Kuh Sung Co., No.1 Szechuen Road, and is at present unemployed.
On December 13, 1937, I introduced him to Mr. Zung Tsing (程俊),
who is a clerk in the Customs Employees Club, Dong Yih Li,
Bubbling Well Road, and a member of the Shanghai Vocational
Circles National Salvation Association. On the instructions
of Zung Tsing, Tseu Zung Teh on 15/12/37 went to Room 218
Bubbling Apartments, Bubbling Well Road, and collected at that
address funds raised by members of the Association.
On December 14, 1937, when I was discharged by the Van

以下为李增裕（Lee Tseng Yue [注：供词中自称为 Zee Tseng Yue，即徐振裕/周成德案中的 Zee Tseng-yue]）之供词，籍贯宁波，由本人 D.J. McKeown 于 1937 年 12 月 30 日在成都路捕房录取，并由书记员 Liao Chung Chien 担任翻译。

本人名叫徐振裕（Zee Tseng Yue），现年 21 岁，籍贯宁波，未婚。
本人失业，此前在爱多亚路 120 号萬豐（Van Foong）粮行担任职员，因行业萧条于 1937 年 12 月 14 日离职。
本人居住在静安寺路静安公寓 218 室，于 12 月 27 日搬至该地址。

本人于 1937 年 8 月加入职业界救国会，当时会址位于重庆路兴权小学。本人也是民国路粮业职工联益俱乐部会员，该俱乐部在中国军队撤离上海后解散。

虽然本人是职业界救国会会员，但除 1937 年 9 月和 10 月分别两次代表该会向亲友募捐外，并未参与其活动。

本人的朋友周成德（Tseu Zung Teh）此前受雇于四川路 1 号库松公司，目前失业。
1937 年 12 月 13 日，本人将他介绍给程俊（Zung Tsing [音译]）先生，程君是静安寺路东义里海关职工俱乐部的职员，也是上海职业界救国会会员。根据程俊的指示，周成德于 1937 年 12 月 15 日前往静安寺路静安公寓 218 室，并在该地址收取了该会会员募集的资金。

1937 年 12 月 14 日，当本人被萬丰

- 2 -

Foong Cereal Hong, I went to live with one Wu Tah Ming (鄔達明)
and Tseu Zung Teh (周成德), both of whom are my friends, at
No.110 Avenue Edward VII. I had at the time a sum of $70.00
which I had saved from my monthly wages. I have spent about
$14.00 for food and locomotion during the past fifteen days
and have at present $56.00 in hand.

While Tseu Zung Teh attended the Bubbling Well Apartments
daily, I went out to call on my friends and relatives with a
view to securing employment. At the same time I also approach-
ed one Aung Tse Tsang (汪子章), an employee of the Yung Dah
Cereal Hong, Rue Montauban, with the object of organizing a
food and fuel supply agency.

On December 16, Tseu and Wu had a quarrel over money and
consequently I and Tseu removed to a room above the Keng Jing
Li (耕莘里) Alleyway, Weihaiwei Road, where we resided up
to December 27 when we went to reside in Room 218 Bubbling Well
Apartments.

Room No.218 was also shared by two other persons, one
named Wong Loo Vung (王魯文), while the name of the other
I do not know. They had resided in the room before we removed
there. I know that Wong Loo Vung was employed in a certain
refugee camp. I had not had much conversation with him because
I used to go out during the day to see my friends and relatives.

I am not so much interested in the national salvation
movement as my employment and I do not know what activities
the Vocational Circles National Salvation Association is
undertaking.

(Signed) Zee Tseng Yue.

粮行解雇时，本人前去与两位朋友鄔達明（Wu Tah Ming）和周成德（Tseu Zung Teh）同住，地址为爱多亚路 110 号。当时本人有一笔从月薪中积攒下来的 70.00 元存款。在过去十五天里，本人花费了约 14.00 元用于食物和交通，目前手头尚有 56.00 元。

当周成德每天前往静安公寓时，本人外出拜访亲友，旨在寻找工作。同时，本人还接触了蒙脱班路（Rue Montauban，今梦花街）永大粮行雇员汪子章（Aung Tse Tsang [音译]），目的是组织一个食品燃料供应机构。

12 月 16 日，周成德和鄔達明因金钱问题发生争吵，因此本人和周成德搬至威海卫路耕莘里（Keng Jing Li [原文拼写与前文略有不同]）弄堂楼上的房间，我们一直居住到 12 月 27 日，随后搬至静安公寓 218 室。

218 室还有另外两人合住，一人名叫王魯文（Wong Loo Vung），另一人姓名本人不知。在我们搬去之前，他们就已居住在该房间。本人知道王魯文受雇于某个难民营。本人与他交谈不多，因为本人白天常外出拜访亲友。

相较于救国运动，本人更关心就业问题，且不知道职业界救国会正在进行什么活动。

（签名）徐振裕（Zee Tseng Yue）。

The following is the statement of Wong Yih ( 王 乙 ) alias Wong Ai yue
(王衡義)
native of Shing Hwa(新化), Kiangsu taken by me D.S. McKeown.
at Chengtu Rd. Stn. on the Dec. 30, 1937 and interpreted by Clerk Zung.

My name is Wong Yih alias Wong Ai Yue. I am 24 years
of age, a native of Shing Hwa(新化), Kiangsu, single,
and unemployed at present. I am living at the Refugee
Camp Workers' Lien Nyi Society, Room 218 Bubbling Well
Apartments, Bubbling Well Road.

Prior to the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities,
I was employed in the King Nyi(景藝) Flower Shop, 400
Tiendong Road, and shortly after the outbreak of the
hostilities, I went to my native place, Shing Hwa, Kiangsu,
as the shop suspended business.

On December 24, I returned to Shanghai as I believed
that the shop would reopen in the near future. Upon
arrival I went to live with my friend named Wong Mou-vung
(王慕文), at the Refugee Camp Workers' Lien Nyi Society,
room 218, Bubbling Well Apartments, Bubbling Well Road.

I met Wong Mou-vung for the first time about three
months ago, when I was still in Shanghai, in the club of
bank and native bank employees, then situated in room 218
Bubbling Well Apartments, through the introduction of one
Yuan Ching Wei(袁青衛) who was formerly one of my
fellow workers in the Chinese National Goods Emporium,
Continental Bank Building, Nanking Road, and whose
present whereabouts I do not know.

As far as I know, Wong Mou-vung is an officer of the
Refugee Camp Workers' Lien Nyi Society, and undertakes the
education of refugees. Apart from living with him as I
am unable to find some other place, I have no connections
with Wong Mou-vung. I am not engaged in any national

以下为王乙（Wong Yih），又名王衡義（Wong Ai yue），江苏新化人，于1937年12月30日在成都路捕房由本人 D.S. McKeown 录取，并由职员 Zung 翻译的供词。

我叫王乙，又名王衡義。现年24岁，江苏新化人，未婚，目前无业。我居住在静安寺路静安别墅联义社难民收容所工作人员宿舍218室。

在中日战事爆发前，我在提篮桥路400号景藝（King Nyi）花店工作，战事爆发后不久，因花店停业，我便回到了家乡江苏新化。

12月24日，我认为该店不久将重新开业，便返回上海。抵沪后，我前往静安寺路静安别墅218室，与我的朋友王慕文（Wong Mou-vung）同住，此处也是联义社难民收容所工作人员的住所。

我大约在三个月前第一次见到王慕文，当时我还在上海，地点是静安别墅218室的银行及钱庄职员俱乐部，是经袁青衛（Yuan Ching Wei）介绍认识的。袁青衛曾是我在南京路大陆银行大楼中国国货公司的一名同事，目前下落不明。

据我所知，王慕文是联义社难民收容所的一名职员，负责难民的教育工作。除了因为找不到其他地方而与他同住外，我与王慕文没有其他关系。我没有参与任何救国

I admit I was a member of the Shanghai vocational
Circles Association to Save the Nation prior to my departure
for my native place. I was employed in the office of the
association in the Sing Kwai Primary School, Park Road, as
a general duty clerk, and I did not undertake any propaganda

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Loo Chi yuan (羅哲原)
native of Shanghai taken by me D.J. McKeown
at Chengtu Rd Stn on the 30/12/37 and interpreted by Clerk Zung Zoong-oen

My name is Loo Chi Yuan (羅哲原). I am nineteen
years of age, a native of Shanghai, unmarried. I have
been working as an apprentice in the Tsing Yuan Cereal Hong
(駿源豆麥行), upper portion of the Sing Kee Shipping
Hong (新記航運行), Rue du Consulat, French Concession,
for about three years, and I am living there.
About two or three days ago, my friend Zee Tseng-yue
(徐振裕), ex-employee of the Van Foong Cereal Hong,
called on me at my place of employment. He informed me
that he was unemployed and asked me to visit him at Room
218, Bubbling Well Apartments, Bubbling Well Road, whenever
I had time, explaining that he desired to have a conversation
with me. At about 6 p.m., December 30, I left my place of
employment for the Bubbling Well Apartments. Unexpectedly
I was arrested by the Police upon entering Room 218 where
I expected to meet my friend. I do not know the reason of
my arrest, and I have no knowledge of the business that my
friend was doing.

Signed : Loo Chi Yuan

上海公共租界工部局警务处。

以下为羅哲原（Loo Chi yuan），上海人，于1937年12月30日在成都路捕房由本人 D.J. McKeown 录取，并由职员 Zung Zoong-oen 翻译的供词。

我叫羅哲原（Loo Chi Yuan）。现年十九岁，上海人，未婚。我在法租界领事馆路新記航運行（Sing Kee Shipping Hong）楼上的駿源豆麥行（Tsing Yuan Cereal Hong）当学徒已有约三年时间，并居住在那里。

大约两三天前，我的朋友徐振裕（Zee Tseng-yue），前万丰豆麦行职员，到我工作的地方来访。他告诉我他失业了，并请我有空时去静安寺路静安别墅218室找他，解释说他想和我谈谈。12月30日下午6点左右，我离开工作地点前往静安别墅。没想到，当我进入218室准备见朋友时，被警察逮捕。我不知道被捕的原因，也不了解我朋友所做之事。

签名：羅哲原

FORM 40
G.EOM-1-37

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Ling Lien-fang (凌联芳)
native of Shanghai taken by me D.S. McKeown
at Chengtu Rd Stn on the 30/12/37 and interpreted by D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken

My name is Ling Lien-fang, aged 21, a native of
Shanghai and single. I am a partner of the Woo Sung
(和生) Flour Shop, 41 Wuting Road. I am living in
house 65 Chao Ka Jao off Hart Road.

I am not a member of the Vocational Circles
National Salvation Association nor of the Refugee Camp
Workers' Lien Nyi Society.

At 5 p.m., December 29, Tseu Zung-teh (周成德),
a friend of mine, who worked with me as a clerk in the
Kuh Sung Firm, a Japanese cotton yarn exchange agency,
No.1 Szechuen Road, before the local hostilities, came to
the Woo Sung Flour Shop, 41 Wuting Road and asked me to
lend him $10 as capital to enter the coal business.
At that time he told me that he lived in Room 218,
Bubbling Well Apartments, Bubbling Well Road and worked
on behalf of refugees. As to the loan, I promised to try
to get some money for him, and he stated that he would
call on me again at 6 p.m. December 30. At this hour,
however, he failed to turn up. As I could not get any
money for him, I decided to give him a reply. So with my
friend Uo Ching-vung (邹锦文), I went to Room 218,
Bubbling Well Apartments, where we were taken by detectives
to Chengtu Road Station.

Signed : Ling Lien-fang.

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
警务调查报告。

以下为凌联芳（Ling Lien-fang），上海人，于1937年12月30日在成都路捕房由本人 D.S. McKeown 录取，并由高级巡长 Kao Yen-ken 翻译的供词。

我叫凌联芳，21岁，上海人，未婚。我是吴淞路41号和生（Woo Sung）面粉店的合伙人。我居住在赫德路附近的曹家宅65号。

我不是职业界救国会的成员，也不是联义社难民收容所工作人员的成员。

12月29日下午5点，我的朋友周成德（Tseu Zung-teh）来到吴淞路41号和生面粉店。战事发生前，他曾在四川北路1号的久生商行（Kuh Sung Firm，一家日本棉纱交易所代理机构）与我一同担任职员。他向我借款10元作为经营煤炭生意的本金。
当时他告诉我，他住在静安寺路静安别墅218室，从事难民救助工作。关于借款一事，我答应尽力为他筹款，他说他将在12月30日下午6点再来找我。然而到了那个时间，他并未出现。由于我未能筹到钱给他，我决定去给他一个答复。于是我和我的朋友邹锦文（Uo Ching-vung）一起前往静安寺路静安别墅218室，在那里我们被侦探带往成都路捕房。

签名：凌联芳。

30M-37

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Li Nyih-jing (李業勤)
native of Ningpo taken by me D.S. Pitts
at Chengtu Rd Stn on the 30/12/37 and interpreted by D.J.I. Kao yen-ken

My name is Li Nyih-jing, age 21, a native of
Ningpo and single. I am unemployed but was formerly
a clerk in the Kuh Sung Firm, a Japanese cotton yarn
exchange agency, 1 Szechuen Road. I am at present living
in Room 218, Bubbling Well Apartments, Bubbling Well Road.
Following the outbreak of the local hostilities,
I went to Hangchow to take refuge and later to my native
place at Ningpo. On December 11, I returned to Shanghai
with a view to withdrawing my deposits from the Bank of
China and the Yien Nyih Bank. I withdrew $92.46, and
remitted $80 to my uncle in Ningpo, retaining the remainder
in order to open a stall in Shanghai so as to earn a living.
About December 17, I opened a macaroni stall on Wuting Road
in front of the Wu Sung Flour Shop, near Carter Road.
On December 24, as I had lost most of my money, I decided
to close the stall. At that time I lived in the Woo Sung
Flour Shop. During my stay there, one of my friends named
Tseu Zung-teh called on me often. On December 24, as the
room in the flour shop was small, Tseu advised me to stay
with him in Room 218, Bubbling Well Apartments, Bubbling
Well Road, which, he told me, was an office for the relief
of refugees. There I have stayed up to the present.
As there were many persons present in the room during
the day, I remained there only during the night.
I am not a member of the Vocational Circles National
Salvation Association nor of the Refugee Camp Workers' Lien
Nyi Society.

警务调查报告。

以下为李業勤（Li Nyih-jing），宁波人，于1937年12月30日在成都路捕房由本人 D.S. Pitts 录取，并由高级巡长 Kao yen-ken 翻译的供词。

我叫李業勤，21岁，宁波人，未婚。我目前无业，但此前曾在四川北路1号的久生商行（一家日本棉纱交易所代理机构）担任职员。我目前居住在静安寺路静安别墅218室。
本地战事爆发后，我先去杭州避难，随后回到家乡宁波。12月11日，我返回上海，打算从中国银行和益利银行提取存款。我提取了92.46元，汇给在宁波的叔叔80元，留下余款以便在上海开设一个小摊谋生。
大约12月17日，我在靠近卡特路的吴淞路上，在和生面粉店门前开设了一个意大利面摊位。
12月24日，由于大部分资金亏损，我决定关闭摊位。当时我住在和生面粉店。在此期间，我的朋友周成德经常来看望我。12月24日，因为面粉店的房间狭小，周建议我与他同住在静安寺路静安别墅218室，他告诉我那是难民救济办公室。我一直住在那里至今。
由于白天房间里有很多人，我只在夜间住在那里。
我不是职业界救国会的成员，也不是联义社难民收容所工作人员的成员。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
========================
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.
================================

The following is the statement of Oo Ching Wen (鄔錦文)
native of Ningpo ........................................ taken by me D.S. Fitts
at Chen tu Ku Stn on the Dec.30,1937. ........ and interpreted by Clerk Zung.

My name is Oo Ching Wen. I am 19 years of age, a native
of Ningpo, single, and unemployed at present. I am living
at No. 1017 Sinza Road.

Prior to the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities,
I was employed as an inspector of the Shanghai Office of
the Joo P'yer Tax Bureau, No. 230 Dal Mou Deu, Nantao,
but was deprived of employment owing to the hostilities.
As I had nothing to do, I often visited my old friend Ling
Lien Teh (凌聯芳), co-proprietor of the Joo Sung (和生)
Macaroni Shop, at No. 25 Wuting Road. Ling and I were
fellow workers in the Shanghai Cotton Exchange, Avenue
Edward VII, about three years ago.

At 5 p.m., December 30, I again called upon Ling Lien
Teh, at No. 25 Wuting Road. He told me that he was going
to visit Tse Zung Teh (in custody) at Room 218, Bubbling
Well Road, to ask for a loan from him. Tse is also a
friend of mine, as we three were fellow workers in the
Shanghai Cotton Exchange, Avenue Edward VII. Consequently
Ling asked me to accompany him to Tse's place and I
agreed. Upon entering Room 218, Bubbling Well Apartments,
both of us were arrested by the Police. I do not know
the reason of our arrest, and have no knowledge of the
activities of the two friends mentioned above.

(signed) Oo Ching Wen.

以下为鄔錦文（Oo Ching Wen），宁波人 ........................................，于1937年12月30日在成都路捕房由本人 D.S. Fitts 录取，并由职员 Zung 翻译的供词。 ........

我叫鄔錦文。现年19岁，宁波人，未婚，目前无业。我居住在新闸路1017号。

在中日战事爆发前，我在南市大码头230号朱佩尔税务局上海办事处担任稽查员，但因战事而失业。由于无事可做，我经常拜访我的老朋友凌聯芳（Ling Lien Teh），他是吴淞路25号和生（Joo Sung）意大利面店的共同经营者。大约三年前，我和凌曾在爱多亚路上海棉花交易所共事。

12月30日下午5点，我再次前往吴淞路25号拜访凌聯芳。他告诉我，他要去静安寺路218室看望周成德（在押），并向他借款。周也是我的朋友，因为我们三人曾在爱多亚路上海棉花交易所共事。因此，凌请我陪他去周某处，我同意了。进入静安别墅218室后，我们两人均被警察逮捕。我不知道被捕的原因，也不了解上述两位朋友的活动情况。

（签名）鄔錦文。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Loo Fen-lai (盧文瀾)
native of Wei Ping (威遠), Szechuen taken by me J.S. Lakeown
at Chen tu Rd Stn on the 30/12/37 and interpreted by Clerk Loi Fei-hong;

My name is Loo Fen-lai, age 23, native of Wei Ping,
Szechuen, residing in the Tsin Tung (運通) Steamship
Company, North Soochow Road. My father died when I
was twelve years of age. When I was six years old, I
commenced studying Chinese under a tutor. I went to the
High Primary School established by the Mission Government
at my native place, at the age of 13. After two years,
I continued my study in the Junior Middle School, also
established by the Mission Government at my native place.
Owing to the fact that my family was poor, I went to the
Southern Szechuen Academy at Looshow (瀘州), Szechuen,
where the tuition was free. I graduated from that school
at the age of 21, and then became a teacher of the Zoong
Yee Primary School (崇義小學) at Loochow. I held this
position for half a year, after which I returned to my
native place with a view to seeking better employment,
but failed. I remained idle at home for about ten months,
until May, 1933, when I left for Chengtu, with a view to
carrying on my study in the Szechuen University, but I
abandoned this decision because I learned that the Ming
Sung Steamship Company was in need of employees. I passed
the examination for my employment, and was despatched in
August, 1933 to the General Office of the Company at
Chungking, at a monthly pay of $8.00. Being dissatisfied,
I resigned after six months, and came to Shanghai in March,
1934 by a steamer of the Ming Sung Company, free of charge
(employees of the Company were entitled free passage).

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
警务调查报告。

以下为盧文瀾（Loo Fen-lai），四川威遠人，于1937年12月30日在成都路捕房由本人 J.S. Lakeown 录取，并由职员 Loi Fei-hong 翻译的供词；

我叫盧文瀾，23岁，四川威遠人，居住在苏州河北路的運通（Tsin Tung）轮船公司。我十二岁时父亲去世。六岁时，我开始跟随塾师学习中文。十三岁时，我进入家乡由教会政府创办的高等小学就读。两年后，我继续在家乡同样由教会政府创办的初级中学学习。由于家境贫寒，我去了四川瀘州的川南学院，那里免收学费。我二十一岁时从该校毕业，随后成为瀘州崇義小學（Zoong Yee Primary School）的教师。我担任此职半年，之后为了寻找更好的工作回到家乡，但未成功。我在家闲居了大约十个月，直到1933年5月，我前往成都，打算在四川大学继续学业，但因得知民生轮船公司需要雇员而放弃了这一决定。我通过了入职考试，并于1933年8月被派往该公司驻重庆的总办事处，月薪8元。因不满意，我在六个月后辞职，并于1934年3月乘坐民生公司的轮船免费（公司员工享有免费乘船待遇）来到上海。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of ............................................................
native of....................................................taken by me....................................
at....................................on the....................................and interpreted by....................................
- 2 -

Upon arrival, I resided at the upper kitchen room, 3 Rue
Chin; Li, Avenue Foch, the home of my friend Mr. Tu Tsao-
yien (杜祝顏), who was an employee of the Sun; San
Cultural Institute (中山文化教育館 ), Avenue Foch.
About twenty days later, in April, I left my friend for
Nankin with a view to studying in the Central Political
Academy. I remained in Nankin for about three months
during which I prepared for examination to join the
academy, and Mr. Tu remitted me $20.00 each month for
my expenses. As a failed in the examination, I returned
to Shanghai in July, and resided with Mr. Tu Tsao-yien.
Shortly after my return to Shanghai, I participated in the
examination for joining the Mongolian and Tibetian Institute,
Lunghwa. I succeeded in the examination and studied for
two years. I graduated in the summer of 1935, and became
a teacher of the Ming Tse (明志) Primary School, Leichow
Road. I held this position until the outbreak of the local
Sino-Japanese hostilities.

After the commencement of the local conflict, I
served as a teacher for juvenile refugees in the camp
established in the Empire Theatre, French Concession, under
the auspices of the Szechuen Fellow Countrymen's Association.

Shortly before the withdrawal of the Chinese troops
from Shanghai, the refugee camp was closed owing to
financial difficulty, consequently I was rendered idle.

Regarding the leaflet entitled "General Outline
of Work during the Propaganda Period," which was seized

以下为 ............................................................（籍贯....................................................）之陈述，由本人....................................于....................................在....................................录取，并由....................................翻译。
- 2 -

抵达后，我居住在福煦路（Avenue Foch）金神父路（Rue Chin; Li）3号楼上厨房房间，此为我朋友杜祝顏先生（Tu Tsao-yien）的住所，他是福煦路中山文化教育館（Sun; San Cultural Institute）的职员。约二十天后，即四月份，我离开朋友前往南京，意在进入中央政治学校求学。我在南京停留了约三个月，期间准备参加该校的入学考试，杜先生每月汇给我20.00元作为生活费。因考试落榜，我于七月返回上海，并与杜祝顏先生同住。

回到上海后不久，我参加了位于龙华的蒙藏学院（Mongolian and Tibetian Institute）的入学考试。我通过了考试并学习了两年。我于1935年夏季毕业，随后成为雷士德路（Leichow Road）明志小学的教师。我一直担任此职，直至本地中日战事爆发。

本地冲突开始后，我在法租界大戏院（Empire Theatre）内设立的难民营中担任难民儿童教师，该营由四川同乡会主办。

在中国军队撤离上海前不久，该难民营因财政困难而关闭，因此我失业。

关于被警方从我处查获的题为《宣传时期工作大纲》的传单，

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of....................................................................................................
native of....................................................................................taken by me............................................................
at........................................on the................................................and interpreted by....................................................

- 3 -

From me by the Police, I have to state that it was issued
to me by one Lin, Iih-sin; (林一心), with whom I
became acquainted recently through the introduction of
my friend Mr. Liu Vong-yuen (刘望远), who is also a
native of Kiangsi. I met Lin; several times on the streets
after the removal of the hostilities from Shanghai, and
requested him to assist me in seeking employment in refugee
camps, but up to the present, he has not recommended me to
any camp. He, however, told me during one of our meetings
on the street to call upon him at 77 Tsingtao Road. I went
to see Lin; at this address, on or about December 22 for the
purpose of getting a reply in connection with my request
for his assistance in securing employment in camps, when he
delivered to me the leaflet without instructions.

I have not participated in any activities conducted
by local national salvation associations, except during the
progress of the local hostilities, I solicited contributions
from my fellow provincials towards the fund for the purchase
of comforts for Chinese soldiers. The contribution
soliciting movement was carried out in the name of the Jui
Tse Study Society (求智读书会) formed by members of
the refugee camp including Mr. Liu Vong-yuen and I myself,
at the request of the members of the Vocational Circles'
National Salvation Association during their visit at our
refugee camp to console refugees. Approximately $80.00
were raised and delivered to the Association in question.

I am not a member of the Communist Party, nor a Kuomintang
member.
Signed : Loo Wen-lai.

警务调查报告。

以下为....................................................................................................（籍贯....................................................................................）之陈述，由本人............................................................于........................................在................................................录取，并由................................................翻译。

- 3 -

我必须声明，该传单是由林一心（Lin, Iih-sin）发给我的。我是通过我的朋友刘望远先生（Liu Vong-yuen，亦为江西人）的介绍最近才认识林的。在上海战事平息后，我曾在街上多次遇见林，并请他协助我在难民营中寻找工作，但至今他未将我推荐至任何难民营。然而，他在我们的一次街头会面中告诉我，让我去青岛路77号找他。大约在12月22日，我去该地址见林，目的是就我请求他协助在营区就业一事获得答复，当时他将该传单交给我，并未附带任何指示。

除在本地战事进行期间外，我未参与任何本地救国会组织的活动。在此期间，我曾向同乡募捐，用于购买慰问中国士兵的物品。这次募捐活动是以“求智读书会”的名义进行的，该会由包括刘望远先生和我自己在内的难民营成员组成，应职业界救国会成员在访问我们难民营慰问难民时的要求而成立。共筹集约80.00元，并交付给该会。

我不是共产党党员，也不是国民党党员。
签名：罗文来（Loo Wen-lai）。

FORM 40
C.M-1-17

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of King, Jing (金瑾)
native of Anhwei taken by me J.S. Hoffman
at Central Station on the 30/12/37 and interpreted by J.J.L. Hee Lee Hien.

My name is King Jing, female, aged 23, a native of
Anhwei and single. I am a student of the Great China
University. Following the outbreak of the local
hostilities, I removed from the school to the residence
of my school mate named Miss Yu Sai-hua (余佩華),
54 (?) Route Delfus. About a month ago, Miss Yu went to
Amoy, and I therefore went to live with a friend of
Miss Yu, named Ho Ying (何英), in the room above the
kitchen at 77 Tsingtao Road.

During my stay in that house, I noticed that a
number of persons visited the kitchen occupied by one
Tsu (朱) and that from conversations among themselves
I realized that they were national salvation workers.
I was afraid that by talking about them, I was of the
opinion that should the police take action against the
occupants of the kitchen, the authorities might suspect us,
I being a student, to be connected with them. Therefore we
agreed that we should claim to be relatives. This is why
we claimed to be relatives when we were taken into the
police station.

Regarding Lin; Yih-sing (林一心), Lin; was one
of the visitors of Tsu. I saw Lin; about two or three
times. He wears spectacles, is of medium size, wears
foreign dress, and speaks Szechuen dialect. I did not see
him bring or take any books. I observed him talking
with Tsu.

I do not know to whom the male clothing, etc.,

C.M-1-17

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
警务调查报告。

以下为金瑾（King, Jing）（安徽人）之陈述，由本人 J.S. Hoffman 于1937年12月30日在中央车站录取，并由 J.J.L. Hee Lee Hien 翻译。

我叫金瑾，女，23岁，安徽人，未婚。我是大夏大学的学生。本地战事爆发后，我从学校搬到我同学余佩華小姐（Miss Yu Sai-hua）的住处，地址为德尔福斯路（Route Delfus）54号（?）。大约一个月前，余小姐去了厦门，因此我去与余小姐的一位朋友何英（Ho Ying）同住，住在青岛路77号的楼上厨房房间。

在我居住在那所房子期间，我注意到有许多人拜访由一位姓朱（Tsu）的人占用的厨房，并且从他们之间的谈话中，我意识到他们是救国工作者。我担心如果谈论他们，一旦警方对厨房居住者采取行动，当局可能会怀疑身为学生的我与他们有牵连。因此我们商定声称是亲戚关系。这就是为什么我们在被带进警察局时声称是亲戚的原因。

关于林一心（Lin; Yih-sing），林是朱的访客之一。我见过林大约两三次。他戴眼镜，中等身材，穿西装，说四川话。我没看到他带来或拿走任何书籍。我观察到他在与朱交谈。

我不知道男性衣物等物品属于谁，

FORM 40

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Ho Ping (何平) alias Ho Yin (何英).
native of Hankow taken by me D. J. McKeown
at Shentu Rd Stn. on the 31/12/1937 and interpreted by D. S. I. Kuo Yen-ken.

My name is Ho Ping alias Ho Yin, aged 26, a native
of Hankow and married. I am a school teacher by profession,
being a teacher in the Yangtsepoo Social Centre Primary
School, Yangtsepoo Road, prior to the hostilities. I
am living in 77 Tsingtao Road.

I am now serving in the Women's Class of the 7th
Hankow Fellow Countrymen's Association, Myburgh Road, near
Avenue Road. This class is opened by an "Education 普及教育服務團
Developing Service Group", which was formed following the
outbreak of hostilities and aimed at national salvation
work. The Group, with an office at 77 Tsingtao Road, was
declared dissolved when the Chinese troops withdrew from the
Shanghai area. It, however, continues to function
secretly at the same address. At first I was paid $10
per month without lodging, but at present I am paid $6
with free lodging at 77 Tsingtao Road. I am paid by Ling
Th-sing (林一心), one of the leading members of the Group.
There are about 40 workers operating in about 20 classes
known as "Children's classes" or "Women's classes".

Tsu Shih-tung (朱澤東), a male youth of about 20,
is the man watching the place and receiving letters and
messages.

Ling Th-sing visits the place, 77 Tsingtao Road, from
time to time. His whereabouts is not known.

In the women's class I am teaching, I was instructed
to teach things in connection with the national salvation
before the withdrawal of the Chinese troops, but after the
page_data.zh:
表格 40
30M-1-37

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
警务调查报告。

以下为何平（Ho Ping），又名何英（Ho Yin）（汉口人）之陈述，由本人 D. J. McKeown 于1937年12月31日在申通路站（Shentu Rd Stn.）录取，并由 D. S. I. Kuo Yen-ken 翻译。

我叫何平，又名何英，26岁，汉口人，已婚。我的职业是学校教师，战事前我在杨树坡社会中心小学（Yangtsepoo Social Centre Primary School，位于杨树坡路）任教。我现居住在青岛路77号。

我目前在迈尔西爱路（Myburgh Road，近爱文义路 Avenue Road）第七汉口同乡会的女子班服务。该班级由一个“普及教育服務團”开办，该团是在战事爆发后成立的，旨在进行救国工作。该团在青岛路77号设有办事处，在中国军队撤离上海地区时被宣布解散。然而，它仍在同一地址秘密运作。起初我月薪10元，不包住宿，但目前我月薪6元，并在青岛路77号免费住宿。我的薪水由该团的主要成员之一林一心（Ling Th-sing）支付。大约有40名工作人员在约20个被称为“儿童班”或“女子班”的班级中工作。

朱澤東（Tsu Shih-tung），一名约20岁的男青年，是负责看守地方并接收信件和消息的人。

林一心（Ling Th-sing）不时访问青岛路77号这个地方。他的行踪不明。

在我执教的女子班中，在中国军队撤离之前，我被指示教授与救国有关的内容，但在

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No.
Section 1, Special Branch.
REPORT
Date December 30, 1937.
Subject. National Salvation Propaganda in Refugee Camps.
Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang. Forwarded by C. Crawford D.S.

Information has been received to the effect that local national salvation elements are making use of refugee camps for the dissemination of propaganda of a national salvation nature and that a number of junior members of this movement are either custodians or staff members of these camps. As a means of cloaking their activities and avoiding the attention of the authorities, a new organization entitled "The Refugee Camp Workers' Lien Nyi Society (难民营工作人员联谊社)" has been formed with a main rendezvous in the 69th Camp which is located in the Chinese National Goods Emporium, Continental Bank Building, 487 Nanking Road. Enquiries are proceeding regarding this organization, and any further particulars which may be obtained will form the subject of a further report.

It is further learned that the New Year Greeting Cards and other pamphlets of a national salvation nature, which have been prepared for distribution on New Year's Day (Vide Special Report dated December 28, 1937) are now stored in Room 218, Bubbling Well Apartments, Bubbling Well Road, near Carter Road (Chengtu Road District)

Sih Tse-liang
C. D. I.

D.C. (Special Branch)

（左侧批注：Visit & Send）
（左侧印章：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 30 DEC 1937）
（左下角手写：263 30/12）

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
档案编号
特务科第一节。
报告
日期：1937年12月30日。
主题：难民营内的救国宣传。
制作人：特务侦探 Sih Tse-liang。转呈人：C. Crawford 副督察长。

收到情报称，本地救国分子正利用难民营传播具有救国性质的宣传品，且该运动的一些初级成员是这些难民营的管理员或工作人员。为了掩盖其活动并避免当局的注意，一个新成立的名为“难民营工作人员联谊社”的组织已经形成，其主要联络点位于南京路487号大陆银行大楼内的中国国货公司里的第69难民营。正在对该组织进行调查，任何可能获得的进一步详情将作为后续报告的主题。

另获悉，为在元旦分发而 prepared 的新年贺卡及其他具有救国性质的小册子（参见1937年12月2日的特别报告），目前存放在静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）靠近成都路（Chengtu Road District）的静安别墅（Bubbling Well Apartments）218室。

Sih Tse-liang
特务侦探

副督察长（特务科）
