page_data.en:
December 30, 37.
National Salvation Movement - Arrests and Seizure
of Propaganda

At 3 p.m. December 30, a party of Police from
Chengtu Road under D.I. Hill, D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken and
D.S. McKeown, acting upon the instructions of the
D.C. (Special Branch) visited room 218, 749 Bubbling
Well Road, suspected of being a depot of the national
salvation association. A large quantity of Chinese
flags, anti-Japanese greeting cards, national salvation
propaganda, and a mimeograph machine were seized. The
seizure was removed to the Special Branch and is at
present in process of classification. Present in the
office at the time of the Police visit were three male
Chinese namely :
(1) Wong Ming Yang (王明揚), salesman for the
China National Insurance Company;
(2) Yang Yuan Kong (楊元康), shroff in the employ
of the Foch Rubber Company, 490 Avenue Foch;
(3) Tseu Zung Teh (周成德), unemployed.
These three persons were taken to Chengtu Road Station and
full statements were obtained (copies attached).
The 1st accused Wong Ming Yang, was definitely
connected with the National Salvation Movement. He admits
being formerly a member of the Foreign Owned Firms Chinese
Employees Lien Nyi Society which formed part of the
Vocational Circles National Salvation Association which
was dissolved following the withdrawal of Chinese troops
from Shanghai. He agreed to participate in the revival
of the National Salvation Movement at the request of one
page_data.zh:
1937年12月30日。
救国运动 - 逮捕及没收宣传品

12月30日下午3时，一支由 Hill 督察、郭彦根（Kao Yen-ken）副督察和 McKeown 警佐率领的成都路警局警力，根据特务科副督察长的指令，走访了静安寺路749号218室，该处被怀疑是救国会的仓库。大量中国国旗、抗日贺卡、救国宣传品以及一台油印机被没收。没收物品已被送往特务科，目前正在进行分类。在警方走访时，办公室内有三名中国男子在场， namely :
(1) 王明揚（Wong Ming Yang），中国保险公司推销员；
(2) 楊元康（Yang Yuan Kong），福煦路490号福煦橡胶公司（Foch Rubber Company）的出纳员；
(3) 周成德（Tseu Zung Teh），无业。
这三个人被带到成都路警局，并取得了完整供词（副本附后）。
第一被告王明揚，确与救国运动有关联。他承认曾是外商华员联谊社的成员，该社是职业界救国会的一部分，后者在中国军队撤离上海后被解散。他同意应一人之请求参与救国运动的复兴

page_data.en:
- 2 -

Yang Yien Sin (楊延修), comprador of the Assurance
Franco-Asiatique, Rue Montauban. Yang a person of some
social standing, appears to be a leading light in the
present movement. His residential address is not known.
Wong Ming Yang admitted that he was engaged in delivering
articles including flags and anti-Japanese greeting cards
on behalf of the National Salvation Association.

The second accused Yang Yuan Kong admits having been
a member of the Vocational Circles National Salvation
Association prior to the withdrawal of Chinese troops,
and states that he was requested on December 30 to take
an active part in the movement. His statement that he
has taken no part in the movement is belied by the fact
that he was in the office at the time of the Police visit.

The third accused Tseu Zung Teh states that a
friend found employment for him in the office at room 218,
distributing cotton vests at a monthly wage of $6.00.
Later he states that a person in the office told him to
distribute 300 greeting cards and 3,000 Chinese National
Flags to all who applied for them. Although Tseu denies
all knowledge of the organization, he is of average
intelligence and doubtless realized the importance of the
work in which he was engaged.

Consequent upon detectives being left to maintain a
seven
watch over the premises, eight male Chinese were arrested
between 6 p.m. and 12 midnight, December 30, namely :
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

杨延修（Yang Yien Sin），蒙托邦路（Rue Montauban）法亚保险公司（Assurance Franco-Asiatique）买办。杨具有一定社会地位，似乎是当前运动中的核心人物。其居住地址不详。黄明阳（Wong Ming Yang）承认，他受救国会委托，从事递送包括旗帜和抗日贺年卡在内的物品的工作。

第二名被告杨元孔（Yang Yuan Kong）承认，在中国军队撤退前曾是职业界救国会的成员，并称他在12月30日被要求积极参与该运动。他声称自己未参与该运动，但警方造访时他正身处办公室内，这一事实戳穿了他的谎言。

第三名被告周成德（Tseu Zung Teh）称，一位朋友为他在218室谋得一份差事，负责分发棉背心，月薪6.00美元。随后他又称，办公室里有人指示他向所有申请者分发300张贺年卡和3,000面中国国旗。尽管周否认对该组织有任何了解，但他智力中等，无疑意识到他所从事工作的重要性。

由于侦探被留下对该处所进行严密监视，12月30日下午6时至午夜12时之间，八名中国男子被捕，名单如下：

page_data.en:
- 3 -

(4) Zee Tseng Yue (徐振裕), unemployed;
(5) Wong Yih (王乙), alias Wong Ai Yue
( ), unemployed;
(6) Loo Chi Yuan (羅哲原), apprentice;
(7) Ling Lien-fang (凌聯芳), partner in a flour
shop;
(8) Li Nyih-jing (李業勤), unemployed;
(9) Oo Ching-wen (鄔銘文), unemployed;
(10) Loo Wen-lai (盧文瀾). unemployed.

The 4th accused Zee Tseng Yue admits having joined
the Vocational Circles National Salvation Association in
August, 1937 but states that his activities were confined
to the collection of funds from friends or relatives on
behalf of the association in September and October, 1937.
He denies that he is taking any part in the present movement,
stating that he was merely residing in room 218, but this
statement is open to doubt from the fact that he was a
former member and found in the office with propaganda much
in evidence. Zee Tseng Yue mentions the name of one
Zung Tsing (程俊), address unknown, clerk in the Customs
Employees Club as being a member of the Vocational Circles
National Salvation Association.

The 5th accused Wong Yih, alias Wong Ai Yue admits
that prior to the outbreak of hostilities, he was a member
of the Vocational Circles National Salvation Association
and was employed in the office of the association. He
states that he was merely residing with friends in room 218,
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

(4) 徐振裕（Zee Tseng Yue），无业；
(5) 王乙（Wong Yih），化名王爱岳（Wong Ai Yue）（原文不清），无业；
(6) 罗哲原（Loo Chi Yuan），学徒；
(7) 凌联芳（Ling Lien-fang），面粉店合伙人；
(8) 李业勤（Li Nyih-jing），无业；
(9) 邬铭文（Oo Ching-wen），无业；
(10) 卢文澜（Loo Wen-lai），无业。

第四名被告徐振裕承认曾于1937年8月加入职业界救国会，但称其活动仅限于1937年9月和10月代表该会向亲友募集资金。他否认参与当前的运动，声称自己 merely 居住在218室，但鉴于他是前成员，且在办公室内被发现存有大量宣传品，这一说法令人怀疑。徐振裕提到程俊（Zung Tsing，音译）的名字，地址不详，海关职员俱乐部职员，系职业界救国会成员。

第五名被告王乙，化名王爱岳，承认在战事爆发前，他是职业界救国会的成员，并在该会办公室任职。他声称自己只是与朋友一起居住在218室，

page_data.en:
- 4 -

but as in the case of the 4th accused, this statement is
open to doubt.

The 6th accused, Loo Chi Yuan, is a friend of the
4th accused, and visited room 218. He denies that he is
participating in the National Salvation Movement.

The 7th accused denies that he is participating
in the movement. He is a friend of the 3rd accused,
Tseu Zung Teh and explains his visit to room 218 by
stating that a loan was being contracted.

The 8th accused Li Nyih-jing (as in the case of the
7th accused), states that he is a friend of the 3rd accused,
and was invited to reside in room 218. He denies that he
is participating in any activities.

The 9th accused Oo Ching Wen is known to the 3rd
and the 7th accused, but denies that his visit to room 218
had any untoward significance.

The arrest of the 10th accused Loo Wen-lai appears
to be of particular importance inasmuch as his examination
and the documents in his possession lead to the belief of
the recrudescence of communism. His statement is typical
of those previously obtained from members of the Communist
Party and documents in his possession which have not yet
been translated are not those ordinarily found on members
of National Salvation organizations.

Of immediate importance is a mimeographed document
entitled "General Outline of Work during the Propaganda
Period," a translation of which follows :-
page_data.zh:
- 4 -

但与第四名被告的情况一样，这一说法令人怀疑。

第六名被告罗哲原是第四名被告的朋友，曾到访218室。他否认参与救国运动。

第七名被告否认参与该运动。他是第三名被告周成德的朋友，并解释称他去218室是为了办理一笔贷款。

第八名被告李业勤（如同第七名被告的情况）称，他是第三名被告的朋友，受邀居住在218室。他否认参与任何活动。

第九名被告邬铭文为第三和第七名被告所认识，但他否认其到访218室有任何不良意图。

第十名被告卢文澜的逮捕似乎尤为重要，因为对他的审讯及其随身携带的文件使人相信共产主义死灰复燃。他的供词具有此前从共产党成员那里获得的供词的典型特征，而他随身携带的尚未翻译的文件并非通常在救国组织成员身上发现的那些文件。

眼下重要的是的一份油印文件，题为《宣传期间工作大纲》，译文如下：

page_data.en:
- 5 -

(1) Political Mobilization prior to the Movement:
The conference will decide the number of members
to be mobilized for the propaganda movement, fund
raising campaign, and consolation movement.
(Three persons to form a group).
The Cultural Circles National Salvation Association
will print propaganda matters for distribution
among organizations.
(2) The work during the Propaganda Period :
General
Proceed with the fund raising campaign for the
relief of refugees.
Enforce anti-Japanese propaganda.
Persuade all shops to hoist national flags
on New Year Day.
Distribute paper slogans on New Year Day among
relatives, friends in shops, alleyways, schools
and refugee camps.
Prepare wall papers.
Hold separate meetings in schools, shops,
refugee camps, factories, take oaths not to
become traitors, not to purchase Japanese goods.
Distribute New Year Cards of an anti-Japanese
nature.
At 10 a.m. New Year Day, mobilize members, to
go to various alleyways and streets and shout slogan
"Long Live the Republic of China!"
page_data.zh:
- 5 -

(1) 运动前的政治动员：
会议将决定为宣传运动、募捐运动和慰劳运动动员的成员人数。（三人组成一个小组）。
文化界救国会将为在各组织中分发而印刷宣传材料。
(2) 宣传期间的工作：
一般事项
开展为难民救济的募捐运动。
推行抗日宣传。
劝说所有商店在元旦悬挂国旗。
在元旦向亲戚、商店里的朋友、弄堂、学校和难民营分发纸质标语。
准备墙报。
在学校、商店、难民营、工厂分别举行会议，宣誓不当汉奸，不购买日货。
分发具有抗日性质的贺年卡。
元旦上午10时，动员成员前往各弄堂和街道，高呼口号“中华民国万岁！”

page_data.en:
- 6 -

(Avoid the appearance of a demonstration).
Mobilize propaganda groups to console wounded
soldiers and refugees during the New Year.
Publish Issue No.3"Unity."
Special
The large Drama Group will stage a drama of a
national salvation nature in a theatre.
The small drama groups will stage dramas in
refugee camps.
Compose songs of a national salvation nature
for refugees.
(3) After the Movement
All sections will hold a conference on January 4th
or 5th to discuss the result of the movement.
The Cultural Circles will convene a meeting of
representatives of all organizations before January 6
to discuss the results.

From information obtained from the 10th accused
between 11 p.m. and 12 m.n., Chengtu Road and Special Branch
detectives visited the home of one named Ling Yih Sing,
77 Tsingtao Road, said to be an important figure
in the National Salvation Movement. Ling was absent but
in the downstairs room, and in an upstairs room reported
by the 10th accused to be tenanted by Ling were found
numerous anti-Japanese books, national salvation propaganda
and a mimeograph machine. This literature is in process of
page_data.zh:
- 6 -

（避免表现出示威的样子）。
动员宣传组在新年期间慰劳伤兵和难民。
出版第三期《团结》。
特别事项
大型剧团将在剧院上演一部救国题材的话剧。
小型剧团将在难民营上演话剧。
为难民创作救国题材的歌曲。
(3) 运动结束后
各部门将于1月4日或5日举行会议，讨论运动结果。
文化界将于1月6日前召集各组织代表开会，讨论结果。

根据12月30日晚11时至午夜12时间从第十名被告处获得的情报，成都路和特务科侦探走访了位于青岛路77号的一名名叫凌亦生（Ling Yih Sing，音译）的人的住所，据说此人是救国运动中的重要人物。凌不在家，但在楼下房间，以及据第十名被告报告由凌租住的楼上房间里，发现了大量抗日书籍、救国宣传品和一台油印机。这些文献正在

page_data.en:
- 7 -

classification. In the upstairs room were found two
females who were brought to the station namely :
(11) King Jing (金瑾), student;
(12) Ho Ping (何平), alias Ho Ying (何英),
school teacher.

The 11th accused, King Jing, when interrogated told
a tissue of lies, contradicting her statements repeatedly.
Although no definite evidence can be produced against her,
she appears to be involved in the National Salvation
Movement.

The 12th accused Ho Ping alias Ho Ying admits that
she was a member of a group which advocates National
Salvation work, and functions secretly at 77 Tsingtao Road.
She was paid by Ling Yih Sing (mentioned above). She
mentions the name of one Tsu Shih-tung (朱澤東), who
is also involved in the movement at the same address.

The ten males and two females are being detained
in Chengtu Road Station pending further instructions.
page_data.zh:
- 7 -

分类整理中。在楼上房间发现两名女性，并被带至警局，名单如下：
(11) 金瑾（King Jing），学生；
(12) 何平（Ho Ping），化名何英（Ho Ying），学校教师。

第十一被告金瑾在接受讯问时谎话连篇，多次自相矛盾。虽然无法提出确凿证据指控她，但她似乎卷入了救国运动。

第十二被告何平，化名何英，承认她是主张开展救国工作的一个团体的成员，该团体在青岛路77号秘密活动。她的薪水由上述凌亦生支付。她提到朱泽东（Tsu Shih-tung）的名字，此人也在同一地址参与该运动。

十名男性和两名女性正拘押在成都路巡捕房，等候进一步指示。

page_data.en:
Wong Yih (王乙) alias Wong Al Yue (王衡遠)
Shing Hwa (兴化), Kiangsu          D.S. McKeown.
Chengtu Rd. Sgn.      30/12/37          Clerk Zung.

My name is Wong Yih alias Wong Al Yue. I am 24 years
of age, a native of Shing Hwa (    ), Kiangsu, single, and
unemployed at present. I am living at the Refugee
Camp Workers' Lien Nyi Society, Room 218 Bubbling Well
Apartments, Bubbling Well Road.

Prior to the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities,
I was employed in the King Nyi (景藝) Flower Shop, 400
Tiendong Road, and shortly after the outbreak of the
hostilities, I went to my native place, Shing Hwa, Kiangsu,
as the shop suspended business.

On December 24, I returned to Shanghai as I believed
that the shop would reopen in the near future. Upon
arrival I went to live with my friend named Wong Mou-vung
(王慕文), at the Refugee Camp Workers' Lien Nyi Society,
Room 218 Bubbling Well Apartments, Bubbling Well Road.

I met Wong Mou-vung for the first time about three
months ago, when I was still in Shanghai, in the club of
bank and native bank employees, then situated in Room 218
Bubbling Well Apartments, through the introduction of one
Yuan Ching Wei (袁青衛) who was formerly one of my
National
fellow workers in the Chinese National Goods Emporium,
Continental Banking Building, Nanking Road, and whose
present whereabouts I do not know.

As far as I know, Wong Mou-vung is an officer of the
Refugee Camp Workers' Lien Nyi Society, and undertakes the
education of refugees. Apart from living with him as I
am unable to find some other place, I have no connections
with Wong Mou-vung. I am not engaged in any national
page_data.zh:
王乙（Wong Yih），化名王衡远（Wong Al Yue）
江苏兴化（Shing Hwa）          D.S. McKeown.
成都路巡捕房      1937年12月30日          书记员 Zung.

我叫王乙，化名王衡远。我今年24岁，籍贯江苏兴化（    ），未婚，目前无业。我住在静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）静安别墅（Bubbling Well Apartments）218室难民劳工联谊社。

在中日战事爆发前，我在天潼路400号景艺（King Nyi）花店工作，战事爆发后不久，因花店停业，我回到了家乡江苏兴化。

12月24日，我认为花店不久将重新开业，便返回上海。抵达后，我去和朋友王慕文（Wong Mou-vung）同住，地址是静安寺路静安别墅218室难民劳工联谊社。

我大约三个月前第一次见到王慕文，当时我还在上海，通过袁青卫（Yuan Ching Wei）的介绍，在南京路大陆银行大楼中国国货公司的一位前同事那里认识的银行和华商银行员俱乐部里见到了他，袁青卫目前的下落我不清楚。

据我所知，王慕文是难民劳工联谊社的职员，负责难民教育工作。除了因为找不到其他地方而与他同住外，我与王慕文没有任何其他联系。我没有从事任何救国

page_data.en:
- 2 -
salvation work at present.
I admit I was a member of the Shanghai Vocational
Circles Association to Save the Nation prior to my departure
for my native place. I was employed in the office of the
Association in the Sing Kwai Primary School, Park Road, as
a general duty clerk, and I did not undertake any propaganda
work. I remained there for about twenty days and then
the association was closed by the Police. After this, I
went to my native place and returned here only recently.
(Signed) Wong Yih.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -
工作。
我承认在离开家乡之前，我是上海职业界救国会的成员。我在公园路星桂小学（Sing Kwai Primary School）的协会办公室担任普通事务 clerk，并未从事任何宣传工作。我在那里待了大约二十天，随后该会被警方关闭。此后，我回到家乡，直到最近才返回这里。
（签名）王乙。

page_data.en:
Loo Chi Yuan (羅哲原)
Shanghai                                      D.S. McKeown
Chengtu Rd Stn          30/12/37          Clerk Zung Zoong-oen

My name is Loo Chi Yuan.    I am nineteen years
of age, a native of Shanghai, unmarried.    I have been
working as an apprentice in the Tsing Yuan Cereal Hong
(駿源豆麥行), upper portion of the Sing Kee Shipping Hong
(新記航運), Rue du Consulat, French Concession, for
about three years, and I am living there.
    About two or three days ago, my friend Zee Tseng-
yue (徐振裕), ex-employee of the Van Foong Cereal Hong,
called on me at my place of employment.    He informed me
that he was unemployed and asked me to visit him at Room
218, Bubbling Well Apartments, Bubbling Well Road, when-
ever I had time, explaining that he desired to have a
conversation with me.    At about 6 p.m., December 30,
I left my place of employment for the Bubbling Well
Apartments.    Unexpectedly I was arrested by the Police
upon entering Room 218 where I expected to meet my friend.
I do not know the reason of my arrest, and I have no
knowledge of the business that my friend was doing.

                                Signed :    Loo Chi Yuan
page_data.zh:
罗哲原（Loo Chi Yuan）
上海                                      D.S. McKeown
成都路巡捕房          1937年12月30日          书记员 Zung Zoong-oen

我叫罗哲原。我今年十九岁，上海人，未婚。我在法租界领事馆路（Rue du Consulat）新记航运（Sing Kee Shipping Hong）楼上的骏源豆麦行（Tsing Yuan Cereal Hong）当学徒已有约三年，并住在那里。
大约两三天前，我的朋友徐振裕（Zee Tseng-yue），万丰豆麦行（Van Foong Cereal Hong）的前雇员，到我的工作地点拜访我。他告诉我他失业了，并请我有空时去静安寺路静安别墅218室找他，解释说他想和我谈谈。12月30日下午6点左右，我离开工作地点前往静安别墅。没想到在进入218室时，我被警察逮捕，我本指望在那里见到我的朋友。我不知道被捕的原因，也不了解我朋友所做的生意。

                                签名：    罗哲原

page_data.en:
Ling Lien Fang (凌联芳)
Shanghai                                      D.S. McKeown
Chengtu Rd Stn           30/12/37             D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken

My name is Ling Lien-fang, aged 21, native of
Shanghai and single. I am a partner of the Woo Sung
(和生) Flour Shop, 41 Wuting Road. I am living in
house 65 Chao Ka Jao off Hart Road.

I am not a member of the Vocational Circles
National Salvation Association nor of the Refugee Camp
Workers' Lien Nyi Society.

At 5 p.m., December 29, Tseu Zung-teh (周成德),
a friend of mine, who worked with me as a clerk in the
Kuh Sung Firm, a Japanese cotton yarn exchange agency,
No.1 Szechuen Road, before the local hostilities, came
to the Woo Sung Flour Shop, 41 Wuting Road and asked me
to lend him $10 as capital to enter the coal business.
At that time he told me that he lived in Room 218,
Bubbling Well Apartments, Bubbling Well Road and worked
on behalf of refugees. As to the loan, I promised to
try to get some money for him, and he stated that he
would call on me again at 6 p.m. December 30. At this
hour, however, he failed to turn up. As I could not
get any money for him, I decided to give him a reply.
So with my friend Oe Ching-vung (郭錦文), I went to
Room 218, Bubbling Well Apartments, where we were taken
by detectives to Chengtu Road Station.

Signed : Ling Lien-fang,
page_data.zh:
凌联芳（Ling Lien Fang）
上海                                      D.S. McKeown
成都路巡捕房           1937年12月30日             D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken

我叫凌联芳，21岁，上海人，未婚。我是吴亭路41号和生（Woo Sung）面粉店的合伙人。我住在赫德路（Hart Road）附近的曹家宅65号。

我不是职业界救国会的成员，也不是难民劳工联谊社的成员。

12月29日下午5点，我的朋友周成德（Tseu Zung-teh）来到吴亭路41号的和生面粉店。战事发生前，他和我一起在四川北路1号的日本棉纱交易所代理行固松洋行（Kuh Sung Firm）做职员。他向我借款10美元作为进入煤炭行业的资本。当时他告诉我，他住在静安寺路静安别墅218室，为难民工作。关于借款，我答应尽力为他筹款，他说他会在12月30日下午6点再来找我。然而，届时他并未出现。因为我没能帮他筹到钱，我决定去给他一个答复。于是我和朋友郭锦文（Oe Ching-vung，音译）一起去了静安寺路静安别墅218室，在那里我们被侦探带到了成都路巡捕房。

签名：凌联芳，

page_data.en:
Li Nyih-jing (李業勤)
Ningpo                                      D.S. Pitts
Chengtu Rd Stn          30/12/37            D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken

My name is Li Nyih-jing, age 21, a native of Ningpo
and single. I am unemployed but was formerly a clerk in the
Kuh Sung Firm, a Japanese cotton yarn exchange agency, No.1
Szechuen Road. I am at present living in Room 218, Bubbling
Well Apartments, Bubbling Well Road.

Following the outbreak of the local hostilities, I
went to Hangchow to take refuge and later to my native place
at Ningpo. On December 11, I returned to Shanghai with a view
to withdrawing my deposits from the Bank of China and the Yien
Nyih Bank. I withdrew $92.46, and remitted $80 to my uncle in
Ningpo, retaining the remainder in order to open a stall in
Shanghai so as to earn a living. About December 17, I opened
a macaroni stall on Wuting Road in front of the Wu Sung Flour
Shop, near Carter Road. On December 24, as I had lost most
of my money, I decided to close the stall. At that time I
lived in the Woo Sung Flour Shop. During my stay there, one
of my friends named Tseu Zung-teh called on me often. On
December 24, as the room in the flour shop was small, Tseu
advised me to stay with him in Room 218, Bubbling Well Apart-
ments, Bubbling Well Road, which, he told me, was an office
for the relief of refugees. There I have stayed up to the
present.

As there were many persons present in the room during
the day, I remained there only during the night.

I am not a member of the Vocational Circles National
Salvation Association nor of the Refugee Camp Workers' Lien Nyi
Society.
page_data.zh:
李業勤 (Li Nyih-jing)
宁波                                      D.S. Pitts
成都路捕房          1937年12月30日            副督察 高延根 (Kao Yen-ken)

本人姓名李業勤，年龄21岁，宁波人，未婚。目前失业，此前曾在四川路1号日本棉纱交易所代理机构“古松洋行”（Kuh Sung Firm）担任职员。现居住于静安寺路静安公寓218室。

本地战事爆发后，我先前往杭州避难，随后回到家乡宁波。12月11日，我返回上海，打算从中国银行和业益银行提取存款。我提取了92.46元，其中80元汇给在宁波的叔父，余款留下以便在上海开设摊位谋生。约在12月17日，我在吴淞面粉店（Wu Sung Flour Shop）前的武定路、靠近卡特路（Carter Road）处开设了一个通心粉摊位。12月24日，由于大部分资金已亏损，我决定关闭摊位。当时我住在吴淞面粉店内。在此期间，我的一位名叫周宗德（Tseu Zung-teh）的朋友经常来看望我。12月24日，因面粉店房间狭小，周建议我与他一同住进静安寺路静安公寓218室，他告诉我那里是一个难民救济办事处。我一直住在那里至今。

由于白天房间里人多，我只在夜间留宿。

我不是职业界救国会的成员，也不是难民营工作人员联义社的成员。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

I know nothing of Tseu Zung-teh(s activities or
private life beyond the fact that prior to the trouble
in Shanghai he worked in the same concern at 1 Szechuen
Road as I did.

Signed : Li Nyih-jing.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

除了知道周宗德（Tseu Zung-teh）在上海出事之前与我同在四川路1号的同一家机构工作外，我对他的活动或私生活一无所知。

签名：李業勤。

page_data.en:
Oo Ching Wen (鄔錦文)
Ningpo                                      D.S. Pitts
Chengtu Rd Stn             30/12/37              Clerk Zung.

My name is Oo Ching Wen. I am 19 years of age,
a native of Ningpo, single, and unemployed at present. I
am living at No. 1017 Sinza Road.

Prior to the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese
hostilities, I was employed as an inspector of the Shanghai
Office of the Joss Paper Tax Bureau, No. 230 Dah Mou Deu,
Nantao, but was deprived of employment owing to the
hostilities. As I had nothing to do, I often visited my
old friend Ling Lien Fang (凌联芳), co-proprietor of the
Woo Sung (和生) Macaroni Shop, at No. 25 Wuting Road.
Ling and I were fellow workers in the Shanghai Cotton
Exchange, Avenue Edward VII, about three years ago.

At 8 p.m. December 30, I again called upon Ling
Lien Fang at No. 25 Wuting Road. He told me that he was
going to visit Tseu Zung Teh (in custody) at Room 218,
Bubbling Well Road, to ask for a loan from him. Tseu is
also a friend of mine, as we three were fellow workers in
the Shanghai Cotton Exchange, Avenue Edward VII. Consequently
Ling asked me to accompany him to Tseu's place and I agreed.
Upon entering Room 218, Bubbling Well Apartments, both of
us were arrested by the Police. I do not know the reason
of our arrest, and have no knowledge of the activities of
the two friends mentioned above.

Signed : Oo Ching Wen;
page_data.zh:
鄔錦文 (Oo Ching Wen)
宁波                                      D.S. Pitts
成都路捕房             1937年12月30日              职员 Zung

本人姓名鄔錦文。年龄19岁，宁波人，未婚，目前失业。居住于新闸路1017号。

在中日敌对行动爆发前，我受雇于南市大码头230号冥币税局上海办事处，担任稽查员，但因战事而失业。由于无事可做，我经常去拜访我的老朋友凌联芳（Ling Lien Fang），他是武定路25号和生（Woo Sung）通心粉店的合伙人。大约三年前，我和凌曾在爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）的上海棉花交易所共事。

12月30日晚8点，我再次到武定路25号拜访凌联芳。他告诉我，他打算去静安寺路静安公寓218室看望周宗德（已被拘留），并向他借款。周也是我的朋友，因为我们三人曾同在爱多亚路的上海棉花交易所共事。因此，凌邀请我陪他去周某处，我同意了。进入静安公寓218室后，我们两人均被警察逮捕。我不知道被捕的原因，也不了解上述两位朋友的活动情况。

签名：鄔錦文；

page_data.en:
Loo Wen-lai ( 盧文來 )
Hyi Ping ( 宜賓 ), Szechuen                      D.S. McKeown
Chengtu Rd. Stn.        30/12/37          Clerk Loh Wei-kong.

My name is Loo Wen-lai, age 26, native of Hyi Ping,
Szechuen, single, residing in the Yuin Tung ( 運通 ) Steamship
Company, North Soochow Road. My father died when I
was twelve years of age. When I was six years old, I
commenced studying Chinese under a tutor. I went to the
High Primary School established by the Hsien Government
of my native place, at the age of 13. After two years,
I continued my study in the Junior Middle School, also
established by the Hsien Government at my native place.
Owing to the fact that my family was poor, I went to the
Southern Szechuen Academy at Leechow ( 州 ), Szechuen,
where the tuition was free. I graduated from that school
at the age of 21, and then became a teacher of the Zoeng
Yee Primary School ( 崇義小學 ) at Leechow. I held this
position for half a year, after which I returned to my
native place with a view to seeking better employment,
but failed. I remained idle at home for about ten months,
until May, 1933, when I left for Chengtu, with a view to
carrying on my study in the Szechuen University, but I
abandoned this decision because I learned that the Ming
Sung Steamship Company was in need of employees. I passed
the examination for my employment, and was despatched in
August, 1933 to the General Office of the Company at
Chungking, at a monthly pay of $8.00. Being dissatisfied,
I resigned after six months, and came to Shanghai in March,
1934 by a steamer of the Ming Sung Company, free of charge
(employees of the Company were entitled free passage).
page_data.zh:
盧文來 (Loo Wen-lai)
四川宜宾 (Hyi Ping, Szechuen)                      D.S. McKeown
成都路捕房        1937年12月30日          职员 Loh Wei-kong

本人姓名盧文來，年龄26岁，四川宜宾人，未婚，居住在苏州北路运通（Yuin Tung）轮船公司。我十二岁时父亲去世。六岁时，我开始跟随塾师学习中文。十三岁时，我进入家乡县政府设立的高等小学就读。两年后，我继续在家乡县政府设立的初级中学学习。由于家境贫寒，我前往四川泸州（Leechow）的川南师范学校，那里免收学费。二十一岁时我从该校毕业，随后成为泸州崇义小学（Zoeng Yee Primary School）的教师。我担任该职半年，之后回到家乡寻求更好的工作，但未成功。我在家闲居约十个月，直到1933年5月，我前往成都，打算在四川大学继续学业，但当我得知民生轮船公司需要雇员时，便放弃了这一决定。我通过了入职考试，并于1933年8月被派往该公司重庆总办事处，月薪8.00元。因不满意，六个月后我辞职，并于1934年3月乘坐民生公司的轮船免费（公司员工享有免费乘船待遇）来到上海。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

Upon arrival, I resided at the upper kitchen room, 3 Yue
Ching Li, Avenue Foch, the home of my friend, Mr. Tu Tsao-
yien (杜祝顏), who was an employee of the Chung San
Cultural Institute (中山文化教育館) Avenue Foch.
About twenty days later, in April, I left my friend for
Nanking with a view to studying in the Central Political
Academy. I remained in Nanking for about three months
during which I prepared for examination to join the
academy, and Mr. Tu remitted me $10.00 each month for
my expenses. As I failed in the examination, I returned
to Shanghai in July, and resided with Mr. Tu Tsao-yien.
Shortly after my return to Shanghai, I participated in the
examination for joining the Mongolian and Thibetan Institute,
Lunghwa. I succeeded in the examination and studied for
two years. I graduated in the summer of 1936, and became
a teacher of the Ming Tse (明志) Primary School, Meichow
Road. I held this position until the outbreak of the local
Sino-Japanese hostilities.

After the commencement of the local conflict, I
served as a teacher for juvenile refugees in the camp
established in the Empire Theatre, French Concession, under
the auspices of the Szechuen Fellow Countrymen's Association.

Shortly before the withdrawal of the Chinese troops
from Shanghai, the refugee camp was closed owing to
financial difficulty, consequently, I was rendered idle.

Regarding the leaflet entitled "General Outline
of Work during the Propaganda Period," which was seized
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

抵达后，我居住在霞飞路（Avenue Foch）月庆里3号楼上厨房房间，那是我的朋友杜祝顏（Tu Tsao-yien）的家，他是霞飞路中山文化教育馆的职员。大约二十天后，即四月，我离开朋友前往南京，打算进入中央政治学校学习。我在南京停留了约三个月，期间准备参加入学考试的复习，杜先生每月汇给我10.00元作为生活费。由于考试落榜，我于七月返回上海，并与杜祝顏先生同住。回到上海后不久，我参加了龙华蒙藏学院的入学考试。我考取并学习了两年。1936年夏毕业，随后成为梅丘路明志（Ming Tse）小学的教师。我一直担任该职，直到本地中日战事爆发。

本地冲突开始后，我在法租界卡尔登大戏院（Empire Theatre）内由四川同乡会主办的难民营中，担任少年难民教师。

在中国军队撤离上海前不久，该难民营因财政困难而关闭，因此我再次失业。

关于被警方从我处搜获的题为《宣传期工作大纲》的传单，

page_data.en:
- 3 -

from me by the Police, I have to state that it was issued
to me by one Ling Yih-sing (林一心), with whom I
became acquainted recently through the introduction of
my friend Mr. Liu Vong-yuen (刘望远), who is also a
native of Szechuen. I met Ling several times on the streets
after the removal of the hostilities from Shanghai, and
requested him to assist me in seeking employment in refugee
camps, but up to the present, he has not recommended me to
any camp. He, however, told me during one of our meetings
on the street to call upon him at 77 Tsingtae Road. I went
to see Ling at this address on or about December 22 for the
purpose of getting a reply in connection with my request
for his assistance in securing employment in camps, when he
delivered to me the leaflet without instructions.

I have not participated in any activities conducted by
local national salvation associations, except during the
progress of the local hostilities, I solicited contributions
from my fellow provincials towards the fund for the purchase
of comforts for Chinese soldiers. The contribution
soliciting movement was carried out in the name of the Jui
Tse Study Society (求智讀書會) formed by members of the
refugee camp including Mr. Liu Vong-yuen and myself, at the
request of the members of the Vocational Circles' National
Salvation Association during their visit at our refugee camp to
console refugees. Approximately $80.00 were raised and
delivered to the Association in question.

I am not a member of the Communist Party, nor a
Kuomintang member.

Signed: Lee Wen-lai.
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

我必须说明，这是林一心（Ling Yih-sing）发给我的。我是通过同为四川人的朋友刘望远（Liu Vong-yuen）先生的介绍，最近才认识林的。上海战事平息后，我在街上见过林几次，并请他协助我在难民营中寻找工作，但至今他未将我推荐至任何难民营。然而，在一次街头会面中，他让我去青岛路77号找他。大约在12月22日，我去该地址见林，目的是就他协助我在难民营就业一事寻求答复，当时他将该传单交给我，并未附带任何指示。

除在本地战事进行期间外，我没有参与任何地方救国会组织的活动。当时，我曾向同乡募集捐款，用于购买慰问中国士兵的物品。这次募捐活动是以“求智读书會”的名义进行的，该会由包括刘望远先生和我在内的难民营成员组成，这是在职业界救国会成员来访难民营慰问难民时提出的要求。共筹集约80.00元，并交付给该会。

我不是共产党党员，也不是国民党党员。

签名：李文来 (Lee Wen-lai)。

page_data.en:
King Jing ( 金瑾 )
Anhwei                                D.S. McKeown
Chengtu Rd. Stn.          30/12/37          D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken

    My name is King Jing, female, aged 23, a native
of Anhwei and single.    I am a student of the Great
China University.    Following the outbreak of the local
hostilities, I removed from the school to the residence
of my school mate named Miss Wu Bai-hwa ( 吴佩華 ),
54(?) Route Dolfus.    About a month ago, Miss Wu went
to Hankow, and I therefore went to live with a friend
of Miss Wu, named Ho Ying ( 何英 ), in the room above
the kitchen at 77 Tsingtao Road.
    During my stay in that house, I noticed that a
number of persons visited the kitchen occupied by one
Chu ( 朱 ) and that from conversations among themselves
I realized that they were national salvation workers.
I and Ho Ying one day talked about them.    I was of the
opinion that should the police take action against the
occupants of the kitchen, the authorities might suspect
us, I being a student, to be connected with them.
Therefore we agreed that we should claim to be relatives.
This is why we claimed to be relatives when we were taken
into the police station.
    Regarding Ling Yih-sing ( 林一心 ), Ling was
one of the visitors of Tsu.    I saw Ling about two or
three times.    He wears spectacles, is of medium size,
wears foreign dress, and speaks Szechuen dialect.    I
did not see him bring or take any books.    I observed
him talking with Tsu.
    I do not know to whom the male clothing, etc.,
which was found in my room belongs, but I think it is
the property of a former tenant who has left for Wuchieh.
    I am not a member of any national salvation society.

                                Signed: King Jing.
page_data.zh:
金瑾 (King Jing)
安徽                                D.S. McKeown
成都路捕房          1937年12月30日          副督察 高延根 (Kao Yen-ken)

    本人姓名金瑾，女性，年龄23岁，安徽人，未婚。我是大夏大学的学生。本地战事爆发后，我从学校搬至同学吴佩華小姐（Miss Wu Bai-hwa）的住所，地址为多福路（Route Dolfus）54号（?）。约一个月前，吴小姐前往汉口，因此我搬去与吴小姐的朋友何英（Ho Ying）同住，地址为青岛路77号楼上厨房房间。
    在该处居住期间，我注意到有许多人拜访由一名朱姓人士（Chu）占用的厨房，并且从他们的交谈中我意识到他们是救国工作者。有一天，我和何英谈论起他们。我认为，如果警察对厨房 occupants 采取行动，当局可能会怀疑身为学生的我与他们有关联。因此，我们商定声称是亲戚关系。这就是为什么我们在被带进警察局时声称是亲戚的原因。
    关于林一心（Ling Yih-sing），林是朱的访客之一。我见过林两三次。他戴眼镜，中等身材，穿西装，讲四川方言。我没见他携带或拿走任何书籍。我观察到他在与朱交谈。
    我不清楚在我房间发现的男装等物品属于谁，但我认为那是以前租客的财产，该租客已前往武昌。
    我不是任何救国会的成员。

                                签名：金瑾。

page_data.en:
Zee Tseng Yue (曾振岳)
Ningpo                                      D.S. McKeown
Chengtu Rd. Stn.    30/12/37                Clerk Liao Chung Chie

My name is Zee Tseng Yue, aged 21, native of Ningpo, single
I am unemployed, formerly working as a clerk in the Van Foong
(万丰) Cereal Hong, 120 Avenue Edward VII, and leaving the
employment on December 14, 1937 owing to trade depression.
I reside in Room 218, Bubbling Well Apartments, Bubbling Well
Road to which address I removed on December 27.

I joined the Vocational Circles National Salvation
Association in August 1937 when it was situated in the Sing
Kwan Primary School, Chungking Road. I was also a member of
the Cereal Hong Employees Lien Nyi Club, Min Kuo Road, which was
dissolved after the withdrawal of the Chinese forces from
Shanghai.

Although I was a member of the Vocational Circles National
Salvation Association I did not take part in its activities
except soliciting funds from friends and relatives on its
behalf on two occasions in September and October, 1937, respect-
ively.

My friend Tseu Zung Teh (周宗德) was formerly employed
Kuh Sung Co., No.1 Szechuen Road, and is at present unemployed.
On December 13, 1937, I introduced him to Mr. Zung Tsing (宗信)
who is a clerk in the Customs Employees Club, Dong Yih Li,
Bubbling Well Road, and a member of the Shanghai Vocational
Circles National Salvation Association. On the instructions
of Zung Tsing, Tseu Zung Teh on 15/12/37 went to Room 218
Bubbling Apartments, Bubbling Well Road, and collected at that
address funds raised by members of the Association.

On December 14, 1937, when I was discharged by the Van

本人姓名曾振岳，年龄21岁，宁波人，未婚。目前失业，此前在爱多亚路120号万丰（Van Foong）粮行担任职员，因行业萧条于1937年12月14日离职。我居住于静安寺路静安公寓218室，于12月27日搬至该址。

我于1937年8月加入职业界救国会，当时该会位于重庆路兴权小学。我也是民国路粮行职员联义俱乐部的成员，该俱乐部在中国军队撤离上海后解散。

虽然我是职业界救国会的成员，但我并未参与其活动，除了在1937年9月和10月分别两次代表该会向亲友募款。

我的朋友周宗德（Tseu Zung Teh）此前受雇于四川路1号的古松公司（Kuh Sung Co.），目前失业。1937年12月13日，我将他介绍给宗信（Zung Tsing）先生，宗先生是静安寺路东益里海关职员俱乐部的职员，也是上海职业界救国会的成员。根据宗信的指示，周宗德于1937年12月15日前往静安寺路静安公寓218室，并在该地址收取该会会员募集的资金。

1937年12月14日，当我被万丰

page_data.en:
- 2 -
Foong Cereal Hong, I went to live with one Wu Tah Ming (鄔達明)
and Tseu Zung Teh (周成德), both of whom are my friends, at
No.110 Avenue Edward VII. I had at the time a sum of $70.00
which I had saved from my monthly wages. I have spent about
$14.00 for food and locomotion during the past fifteen days
and have at present $56.00 in hand.
While Tseu Zung Teh attended the Bubbling Well Apartments
daily, I went out to call on my friends and relatives with a
view to securing employment. At the same time I also approach-
ed one Faung Tse Tsang (馮子章), an employee of the Yung Dah
Cereal Hong, Rue Montauban, with the object of organizing a
food and fuel supply agency.
On December 16, Tseu and Wu had a quarrel over money and
consequently I and Tseu removed to a room above the Keng Sing
Li (耕莘里) Alleyway, Weihaiwei Road, where we resided up
to December 27 when we went to reside in Room 218 Bubbling Well
Apartments.
Room No.218 was also shared by two other persons, one
named Wong Moo Vung (王慕文), while the name of the other
I do not know. They had resided in the room before we removed
there. I know that Wong Moo Vung was employed in a certain
refugee camp. I had not had much conversation with him because
I used to go out during the day to see my friends and relatives.
I am not so much interested in the national salvation
movement as my employment and I do not know what activities
the Vocational Circles National Salvation Association is
undertaking.
(Signed) Zee Tseng Yue.

丰粮行（Foong Cereal Hong），我搬去与邬达明（Wu Tah Ming）和周成德（Tseu Zung Teh）同住，二人均是我的朋友，住址为爱德华七世路110号。当时我有一笔70.00元的积蓄，系从月薪中节省下来。在过去十五天里，我在食物和交通方面花费了约14.00元，目前手头尚有56.00元。

当周成德每日前往静安寺公寓（Bubbling Well Apartments）时，我则外出拜访亲友，以期谋得职位。同时，我也接触了一位冯子章（Faung Tse Tsang），他是蒙托邦路（Rue Montauban）永大粮行（Yung Dah Cereal Hong）的职员，目的是组织一个粮食和燃料供应机构。

12月16日，周和吴因金钱问题发生争吵，因此我和周搬至威海卫路耕莘里（Keng Sing Li）弄堂楼上的一间房间居住，直至12月27日，我们搬至静安寺公寓218室居住。

218室还由另外两人合租，一人名为王慕文（Wong Moo Vung），另一人的姓名我不知道。在我们搬去之前，他们已居住在该房间。我知道王慕文受雇于某难民收容所。我与他交谈不多，因为我白天常外出拜访亲友。

我对救国运动的兴趣不如对就业的兴趣大，我不了解职业界救国会正在进行什么活动。

（签名）Zee Tseng Yue。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Wong Foo Pau (汪府宝).
native of Peiping taken by me D.3. McKeown
at Chengtu Road on the 7/1/38 and interpreted by Clerk Wong Chia-tsing

My name is Wong Foo Pau. I am a native of
Peiping, age 20, residing at Room No.50 Paris Apartments,
Avenue Dubail. I am a student of the Kuo Kwang Middle
School, Avenue Road near Carter Road, having joined
this school in September, 1937. I arrived in Shanghai
from Peiping during the summer last year.

About one months ago I received a letter,
which was addressed to me c/o the Kuo Kwang Middle
School, from one Tsang Vung-ling (張文霖), schoolmate
who left school about one month ago, telling me that if
I needed books to read, I could call on him at 77
Tsingtao Road. At 2 p.m. to-day, I went to 77 Tsingtao
Road for the purpose of borrowing a book entitled "The
Good Earth", a film of this book is showing at the
Nanking Theatre. I knew he had this book when he was
at the school. I do not know Tsang's present position.
On arrival at 77 Tsingtao Road, I was arrested by the
detectives.

I have never been to this address before, and
this is my first visit. I have not participated in
any political societies or their activities.

The above is my true statement.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Further to this case, two more male Chinese were arrested by detectives posted at 77 Tsingtao Road, at 2.30p.m. and 3.30p.m. 3-1-38, respectively:-

1. Wong Moo Vung (王慕文), alias Wong Chi (王起) 23, native of Kiangsu, S/unemployed, No.265 Zeng An Lee, Rue Kraetzer.

2. Ting Vung Sung, (丁文松), age 30, native of Kwangtung, S/unemployed, teacher, Chung Hwa Lodging House (中華) Route de Zikawei.

Statements were taken from both, copies of translations attached hereto, after interrogation by D.S. Larby and D.S.I. Shih Sau Chien.

Resulting from part of the confession of the first above-named he led the said detectives, accompanied by C.D.3. 174 and the undersigned to the Ching Sing (慶星) Printing Shop, 224 Sinza Road, proprietor one Lee Hai Kyung (李海京), said to have been responsible for printing National Flags and Greeting Cards to be distributed to the Camps.

This man, questioned, admitted so doing and agreed that he had destroyed the printing blocks when requested to do so by the 1st above named. He wrote a statement to that effect, translation attached. Premises searched, nothing incriminating found.

The two arrested men are being detained at Chengtu Road Station, awaiting disposal of D.C. (Special Branch).

1. 王慕文（Wong Moo Vung），别名王起（Wong Chi），23岁，江苏籍，单身/无业，住克勒策尔路（Rue Kraetzer）增安里265号。

2. 丁文松（Ting Vung Sung），30岁，广东籍，单身/无业，教师，住徐家汇路（Route de Zikawei）中华旅舍（Chung Hwa Lodging House）。

两人均已被录口供，译文副本附后，由侦探长 Larby 和侦探副督察 石守坚（Shih Sau Chien）审讯。

根据上述第一名男子的部分供词，他带领所述侦探，由刑事侦探三等警员174号及本人陪同，前往新闸路224号庆星（Ching Sing）印刷所，该所老板为李海京（Lee Hai Kyung），据称负责印制将分发至各难民营的国旗和贺年卡。

经讯问，此人承认了上述事实，并同意他在上述第一名男子要求下销毁了印版。他就此写了一份陈述书，译文附后。对该场所进行了搜查，未发现任何罪证。

Wong Moo-vung (王慕文) alias Wong Mu (王起)
Tai Chong (Kiangsu)
Chengtu Ki          Jan. 3, 1938.          .S.I. Shih Hsu-chieh

My name is Wong Moo-vung alias Wong Mu, age 33,
native of Tai Chong (Kiangsu), single, unemployed, residing
with my sister at No. 265 Zang An Lee (長安里), Rue
Krastzer.

I graduated from the Agricultural Normal School,
Tai Chong, in the year of 1934 and came to Shanghai in the
spring of 1936. Between April, 1936 and August, 1937, I
was a teacher of the Soo Soo Primary School (苏小学),
265 Zang An Lee, Rue Krastzer, of which my sister Wong Woo (王和)
was the principle.

Subsequently to the outbreak of the local hostilities,
I became unemployed. Through the introduction of a friend of
mine named Woo Tsung-vung (吴宗文), I joined the Shanghai
Vocational Circles National Salvation Association, Lane 188,
House 4 Park Road and became a staff member attached to the
Refugee Section of the Association. Mr. Pan Yang-yao (潘仰尧),
a Committee member of the above Association, is personally
acquainted with me. He is a fellow native of mine, but I
do not know where he is at present.

When the Shanghai Vocational Circles National
Salvation Association was closed by the Municipal Police
about one month ago, I again became unemployed. Later,
a number of the ex-staff members, including myself, of the
Refugee Section of the Shanghai Vocational Circles National
Salvation Association in conjunction with several supervisors
of various local refugee camps formed the "Staff Members' Hu
Nyi (Mutual Aid) Society of Various Refugee Camps" at Room 218,
page_data.zh:
王慕文（Wong Moo-vung），别名王起（Wong Mu）
太仓（江苏）
成都路警站          1938年1月3日          侦探副督察 石旭杰（Shih Hsu-chieh）

本人名为王慕文，别名王起，现年33岁，籍贯江苏太仓，未婚，无业，与姐姐同住于克勒策尔路（Rue Krastzer）长安里（Zang An Lee）265号。

我于1934年毕业于太仓农业师范学校，并于1936年春来到上海。1936年4月至1937年8月期间，我在克勒策尔路长安里265号的苏苏小学（Soo Soo Primary School）担任教师，该校校长是我的姐姐王和（Wong Woo）。

本地战事爆发后，我失业了。通过我的朋友吴宗文（Woo Tsung-vung）的介绍，我加入了位于派克路（Park Road）4号188弄的上海职业界救国会，并成为该会难民部的一名工作人员。上述协会的委员潘仰尧（Pan Yang-yao）与我私交甚笃。他是我的同乡，但我不知道他目前身在何处。

大约一个月前，上海职业界救国会被工部局警务处关闭，我再次失业。后来，包括我在内的原上海职业界救国会难民部的一些前工作人员，联合当地各难民营的几位监督员，在南京西路（Bubbling Well Road）静安寺大楼（Bubbling Well Building）218室成立了“各难民营职员互助社”（Staff Members' Hu Nyi (Mutual Aid) Society of Various Refugee Camps），

page_data.en:
( 2 )
Building,
Bubbling Well Bubbling Well Road. I was
appointed Secretary of this Society, the object of which was
to promote education among the refugees in various camps.
My fellow workers are named as follows :-
Wang Min-yang ( 王名揚 ).
Chen Da-sun ( 陳達生 ).
Chen Kuo-chuin ( 陳國鈞 ).
Tsai Lai ( 蔡磊 ).
Fan Sze-tseng ( 潘世徵 ).
Wong San-chuen ( 王三川 ).
Ling Yih-sin ( 林一心 ).
The Society is composed of 3 sections, namely
Educational Section, Employment Section and Social Section,
but I am unable to tell who are the responsible members in
charge of the respective sections because they very seldom
put in an appearance at the aforementioned address.
The formation of this Society was entirely for the
welfare of the refugees and for this reason I understand that
Mr. H.C. Chen ( 丁鶴琴 ), Chinese Education Officer of the
S.M.C., expressed his approval of the aims of this Society.
I am personally acquainted with Mr. Chen as a result of my
having worked for the refugees affairs during the past few
months, Mr. Chen being a responsible member in charge of the
Refugee Section of the International Red Cross Committee.
I do not know who brought all the propaganda matter to
the office as I happened to be away from the office on
December 29th, visiting my sister, when the handbills were
page_data.zh:
( 2 )
大楼，
南京西路。我被任命为该社秘书，其宗旨是促进各难民营难民的教育。我的同事名单如下：-
王名揚（Wang Min-yang）。
陳達生（Chen Da-sun）。
陳國鈞（Chen Kuo-chuin）。
蔡磊（Tsai Lai）。
潘世徵（Fan Sze-tseng）。(注：原文拼音为Fan，中文名通常为潘，但也可能是范，此处依常见姓氏译为潘，若严格对应拼音可为范)
王三川（Wong San-chuen）。
林一心（Ling Yih-sin）。
该社分为三个部门，即教育部、就业部和社会部，但我无法告知各部门的负责人是谁，因为他们很少出现在上述地址。
该社的成立完全是为了难民的福利，因此我了解到工部局华务教育处处长陈鹤琴先生（H.C. Chen）对该社的宗旨表示赞同。由于过去几个月我从事难民事务工作，我与陈先生私交甚笃，陈先生是国际红十字会委员会难民部的负责人。
我不知道是谁把所有宣传品带到办公室的，因为12月29日分发传单时，我碰巧不在办公室，而是去探望我的姐姐，当时传单

page_data.en:
( 3 )

delivered. However, I believe that Wong Min-yang was responsible
for printing these handbills with the object of instilling the
inmates of the various refugee camps with feelings of patriotism.

I knew nothing about the Police raid on the Bubbling
Well Building until about 10 a.m. January 1 when I met on
Chengtu Road one Zee Yoch-ching (徐肇慶), who happened to be
near the scene of raid, but he himself is not a member of the
Society. I was very much surprised to learn of the raid by
the Police and to satisfy my curiosity, I proceeded to 77
Tsingtao road to interview one Ling Yih-sin, also a member of
the Society, at 1 p.m. January 3, with the intention to find
out from him why the office of the Society had been raided.
On my arrival at the latter mentioned address I was arrested.

Signed: Wong Moo-yung.

Addendum
Further questioned, the accused made the following
statement :-

On or about Dec.24, I together with Woo Chuen (吳全), a
friend of mine, went to the Ching Sing (精星) Printing Shop at
224 Sinza Rd on instructions of Wong Min-yang, to print 20,000
paper national flags and 20,000 paper slips inscribed with
slogans of a national salvation nature. On Dec.30, we took the
slips and a number of paper flags to the Society's office at
Room 218 Bubbling Well Building, Bubbling Well Road.

When I learned about the raid conducted by the Municipal
Police on the Society's premises, I went to the Ching Sing

Wong San-chuen (王三川).
Ling Yih-sin (林一心).
The Society is composed of 3 sections, namely
Educational Section, Employment Section and Social Section,
but I am unable to tell who are the responsible members in
charge of the respective sections because they very seldom
put in an appearance at the aforementioned address.
The formation of this Society was entirely for the
welfare of the refugees and for this reason I understand that
Mr. H.C. Chen (陳鶴琴), Chinese Education Officer of the
S.M.C., expressed his approval of the aims of this Society.
I am personally acquainted with Mr. Chen as a result of my
having worked for the refugees camps during the past few
months, Mr. Chen being a responsible member in charge of the
Refugee Section of the International Red Cross Committee.
I do not know who brought all the propaganda matter to
the office as I happened to be away from the office on
December 29th, visiting my sister, when the handbills were
page_data.zh:

大楼，
静安寺路静安寺路。我被任命为本会秘书，本会之宗旨为促进各难民营中难民之教育。我的同事名单如下：-
Wong Min-yang (王名揚)。
Chen Dze-sun (陳子孫)。
Chen Kuo-chuin (陳國鈞)。
Tsai Lei (蔡磊)。
Fan Dze-tseng (潘齒徵)。
Wong San-chuen (王三川)。
Ling Yih-sin (林一心)。
本会由三个部门组成，即教育部、就业部和社会部，但我无法告知各部门的负责人是谁，因为他们很少在上述地址露面。
本会的成立完全是为了难民的福利，因此我了解到工部局华务教育处处长 H.C. Chen (陳鶴琴) 先生对本会的宗旨表示赞同。由于过去几个月我在难民营工作，我与陈先生相识，陈先生是国际红十字会难民部负责人。
我不知道是谁将所有宣传品带到办公室的，因为 12 月 29 日传单送达时，我碰巧不在办公室，而是去探望我的姐姐，当时传单

page_data.en:
( 3 )

delivered. However, I believe that Wong Min-yang was responsible
for printing these handbills with the object of instilling the
inmates of the various refugee camps with feelings of patriotism.

I knew nothing about the Police raid on the Bubbling
Well Building until about 10 a.m. January 1 when I met on
Chengtu Road one Zee Yoch-ching (徐聿瑾), who happened to be
near the scene of raid, but he himself is not a member of the
Society. I was very much surprised to learn of the raid by
the Police and to satisfy my curiosity, I proceeded to 77
Tsingtao Road to interview one Ling Yih-sin, also a member of
the Society, at 1 p.m. January 3, with the intention to find
out from him why the office of the Society had been raided.
On my arrival at the latter mentioned address I was arrested.

Addendum                                          Signed: Wong Moo-yung.

Further questioned, the accused made the following
statement :-

On or about Dec.24, I together with Woo Chuen (吴全), a
friend of mine, went to the Ching Sing (鏡星) Printing Shop at
224 Sinsa Rd on instructions of Wong Min-yang, to print 20,000
paper national flags and 20,000 paper slips inscribed with
slogans of a national salvation nature. On Dec.30, we took the
slips and a number of paper flags to the Society's office at
Room 218 Bubbling Well Building, Bubbling Well Road.

When I learned about the raid conducted by the Municipal
Police on the Society's premises, I went to the Ching Sing
Printing Shop and warned the shop master to take care of the
flags for fear the Police might conduct a search for them.
page_data.zh:
( 3 )

交付。然而，我相信黄敏扬（Wong Min-yang）负责印刷这些传单，目的是向各难民营的收容人员灌输爱国情感。

直到1月1日上午10点左右，我在成都路遇到徐聿瑾（Zee Yoch-ching），他对静安寺路大楼遭警方突袭一事并不知情，当时他恰好在突袭现场附近，但他本人并非该会社成员。得知警方进行突袭后，我感到非常惊讶，为了满足我的好奇心，我于1月3日下午1点前往青岛路77号去会见该会社的另一名成员凌一心（Ling Yih-sin），打算从他那里了解该会社办公室为何遭到突袭。当我到达上述地址时，我被逮捕了。

附言                                          签名：黄慕雍（Wong Moo-yung）。

经进一步讯问，被告作出如下陈述：-

大约在12月24日，我按照黄敏扬（Wong Min-yang）的指示，与我的朋友吴全（Woo Chuen）一同前往新闸路224号的镜星（Ching Sing）印刷所，印制2万面纸质国旗和2万张写有救国性质标语的纸条。12月30日，我们将这些纸条和若干面纸质国旗带到了静安寺路静安寺大楼218室的该会社办公室。

当我得知工部局警察对该会社场所进行突袭后，我去了镜星印刷所，警告店主妥善保管旗帜，以免警方搜查。

page_data.en:
( 4 )
My object in so doing was to prevent myself from being
involved in the case, should the Police discover the Printing
Shop.
I don't know where the other handbills and pamphlets
were printed.
page_data.zh:
( 4 )
我这样做的目的是，如果警方发现该印刷所，防止我自己卷入此案。
我不知道其他传单和小册子是在哪里印刷的。

Kwangtung                                      XX D.S. Larby
Changtu Road            Jan. 3, 1938,                  D.S.I. Shih Ssu-chien.

My name is Ting Vung-sung, age 30, native of Hainan,
Kwangtung, single, unemployed, teacher, residing at Chung
Hwa Lodging House ( 中華 ), Route de Zikawei.
    I came to Shanghai on December 22 together with
of hundreds of other refugees from Nanking where I was a
teacher in the Yoch Tsai (育材) Primary School, Nanking.
Before I became a teacher in the Yoch Tsai Primary School
early in 1937, I had been for the past several years a
teacher in various primary schools in Anking, Anhwei.
    As I have no relatives nor funds in Shanghai, I
put up in the Chung Hwa Lodging House, Route de Zikawei, as
soon as I arrived here.
    I have tried very hard to obtain an employment without
success. I then suddenly remembered that my friend Ou Yang
Chao (歐陽超) had often told me about one Fong Hsin-yien
(方兴嚴) as a person who had a large number of friends in
educational circles. I decided to call on him with the
object of requesting him to obtain for me a position as a
teacher. When I did this at about 2.30 p.m. January 3,
I was arrested by detectives on duty inside the premises.
    I have never participated in any anti-Japanese
movement and I am not a member of any national salvation
associations.

                                        Signed: Ting Vung-sung.
page_data.zh:
丁文孫 (Ting Vung-sung)
广东                                      XX D.S. Larby
成都路            1938年1月3日，                  D.S.I. Shih Ssu-chien.

我叫丁文孫，30岁，广东海南人，未婚，失业，教师，居住在霞飞路中华寄宿舍（Chung Hwa Lodging House）。
    我于12月22日与数百名其他难民一起从南京来到上海，我在南京育才（Yoch Tsai）小学担任教师。在1937年初成为育才小学教师之前，过去几年我一直在安徽安庆的各所小学任教。
    由于我在上海没有亲戚也没有资金，我一到这里就住进了霞飞路的中华寄宿舍。
    我非常努力地寻找工作，但没有成功。后来我突然想起我的朋友欧阳超（Ou Yang Chao）经常向我提起方兴嚴（Fong Hsin-yien），说他在教育界有很多朋友。我决定去拜访他，目的是请求他为我谋得一个教师职位。当我在1月3日下午2点30分左右这样做时，我被在该场所内执勤的侦探逮捕。
    我从未参加过任何反日运动，也不是任何救国会社的成员。

                                        签名：丁文孫。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Tsoong Ho-sung (宗荷生).
native of Changchow taken by me D.9.I. Kao Yen-ken
at Chengtu Rd Stn on the 2/1/1938 and interpreted by

My name is Tsoong Ho-sung, aged 27, a native of
Changchow, and single. I now reside in the Tai Lee (泰利)
Refugee Camp, Tai Lee Godown, off North Hokien Road, near
the Bridge. I am a printer by profession, at present being
unemployed.

At the time of the outbreak of the local hostilities,
I was in the employ of the Ming Yih (明益) Printing Works, Kiu
Chao Zang (舊校場), Nantoo, but was later discharged owing to
trade depression. Thereupon I went to live with Sung Yih-ts
(孙一之), a friend of mine, 77 Tsingtao Road, where Sung
owned a Nyi Hwa (藝華) Printing Works. At the beginning
of November, 1937, the printing works was closed because of
financial difficulties. Sung transferred the lease of the
house to one named Fang (方) and returned to Changchow.
He deposited his printing machine in the kitchen pending
removal. At that time, I intended to return to Changchow
with Sung, but without avail due to lack of travelling expenses.
I therefore continued to stay on the premises with the machine.
About two months later (towards the end of December, 1937), the
machine was taken away to an unknown address by a female named
Yang (楊) of the Meng Yang (孟養) Hospital, Burkill Road,
with the permission of Sung Yih-ts. I know that the Nyi
Hwa Printing Works dealt in the printing of packages of toilet
articles and by no means in ordinary printing.

During my stay at 77 Tsingtao Road, I earned my
living by selling cigarettes and sweetmeats on streets and
alleyways. Towards the end of December, 1937, I lost

我叫宗荷生，27岁，常州人，未婚。我现在居住在泰利（Tai Lee）难民营，位于北福建路附近桥边的泰利仓库。我的职业是印刷工，目前失业。

在当地战事爆发时，我受雇于南市旧校场（Kiu Chao Zang）的明益（Ming Yih）印刷厂，但后来因行业萧条而被解雇。随后，我去和我的好朋友孙一之（Sung Yih-ts）同住，地址是青岛路77号，孙在那里拥有一家艺华（Nyi Hwa）印刷厂。1937年11月初，该印刷厂因财务困难而关闭。孙将房屋的租赁权转让给了一位姓方（Fang）的人，并返回常州。他将印刷机存放在厨房里，等待搬走。当时，我打算随孙一起返回常州，但因缺乏旅费而未成行。因此，我继续带着机器留在该场所。大约两个月后（1937年12月底），经孙一之许可，一位来自伯基尔路孟养（Meng Yang）医院的姓杨（Yang）的女子将机器运往一个未知的地址。我知道艺华印刷厂从事的是卫生用品包装的印刷，绝非普通印刷。

Ying Yung-dien (邢永典)。
Paoting                                      D.O.I. Kao Yen-ken
Chengtu Rd Stn             2/1/1938

My name is Ying Yung-dien, aged 26, a native of Paoting
and married. I am residing with my wife and two children
at 787 Amherst Avenue. I only occupy a small room on
the premises, the other rooms being occupied by refugees,
known as the 81st Refugee Camp of the "Refugees' Relief Branch"
of the Disaster Relief Federation. I am an artist by
profession. Prior to the outbreak of the local hostilities
I drew pictures for school text books, etc. for the Tien
Ma (天馬) Bookstore, Honan Road, near Avenue Edward VII,
the Yah Tung (亞東) Bookstore, Foochow Road, and the Er
Dong (兒童) Bookstore, Foochow Road.
On or about December 25, 1937, I called upon Miss Ho
Chung (何中), a school mate of my wife named Chang Li-
ying (張立英) at her residence, 77 Tsingtao Road, with a
view to requesting her to find any available employment for
me. She is a good friend of my wife and they often
visited each other. She promised to approach the
Education Committee of the International Relief Society,
which looks after the education of children, for a position.
At that time, a young man named Tsu (朱) was also present.
He asked me how many refugees were accommodated in the 81st
Refugee Camp and how many child refugees there were. In
reply I told him that there were a total of about 400
refugees, out of which number 150 were children. These
figures were very rough, as I am not an employee of the
refugee camp nor a refugee in it. Tsu stated that he was
working with the above-mentioned Education Committee, that

邢永典（Ying Yung-dien）。
保定                                      侦探科督察 高延根
成都路捕房             1938年1月2日

本人名叫邢永典，现年26岁，保定人，已婚。我与妻子及两名子女居住在爱文义路787号。我在该处仅占用一个小房间，其余房间均由难民居住，此处被称为灾民救济联合会“难民救济分会”的第81难民收容所。我的职业是画家。在当地战事爆发前，我曾为位于爱多亚路附近的河南路天马书店、福州路亚东书店以及福州路儿童书店绘制学校教科书等插图。
1937年12月25日左右，我前往青岛路77号拜访何中女士，她是我妻子张立英的同学。我去的目的是请她为我寻找任何可用的工作机会。她是我妻子的挚友，她们经常互相往来。她答应向国际救济社的教育委员会为我谋求一个职位，该委员会负责儿童教育工作。当时，一位姓朱的年轻男子也在场。他询问我第81难民收容所收容了多少难民，其中有多少儿童难民。我回答说，难民总数约为400人，其中儿童有150人。这些数字非常粗略，因为我既不是收容所的工作人员，也不是其中的难民。朱某表示他在上述教育委员会工作，并且

page_data.en:
- 2 -
he would assist me in getting employment as a teacher to
child refugees in the 81st Refugee Camp, and that in two
or three days, books, a blackboard and chalk would be
sent to me.
As Ho and T'au failed to give me a reply as promised,
I visited 77 Tsingtao Road, again at about 1 p.m. January 2,
when I was arrested by the Municipal Police.
I am not a member of any political organization, nor
have I ever engaged in any national salvation movement. I
am not a Communist.
I know that Ho Chung was a member of the Education
Developing Service Group, which was engaged in national
salvation movement at the time of the local hostilities.
I, however, have no knowledge as to whether the group is
still functioning, because Ho Chung and I have not talked
about the activities of the group since the withdrawal
of the Chinese troops from Shanghai.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -
他将协助我在第81难民收容所获得一份担任儿童难民教师的工作，并说在两三天内会将书籍、黑板和粉笔送给我。
由于何中和陶某未按承诺给我回复，我于1月2日下午1点左右再次前往青岛路77号，随即被工部局警务处逮捕。
我不是任何政治组织的成员，也从未参与过任何救国运动。我不是共产党员。
我知道何中曾是教育发展服务团的成员，该团体在当地战事期间从事救国运动。然而，我不知道该团体是否仍在运作，因为自中国军队撤离上海后，何中与我未曾谈论过该团体的活动。

My name is Tsoong Ho-sung, aged 27, a native of
Changchow, and single. I now reside in the Tai Lee (泰利)
Refugee Camp, Tai Lee Godown, off North Fukien Road, near
the Bridge. I am a printer by profession, at present being
unemployed.

At the time of the outbreak of the local hostilities,
I was in the employ of the Ming Yih (明益) Printing Works, Kiu
Chao Zang (舊校場), Nantao, but was later discharged owing to
trade depression. Thereupon I went to live with Sung Yih-ts
(孫一之), a friend of mine, 77 Tsingtao Road, where Sung
owned a Nyi Hwa (藝華) Printing Works. At the beginning
of November, 1937, the printing works was closed because of
financial difficulties. Sung transferred the lease of the
house to one named Fang (方) and returned to Changchow.
He deposited his printing machine in the kitchen pending
removal. At that time, I intended to return to Changchow
with Sung, but without avail due to lack of travelling expenses.
I therefore continued to stay on the premises with the machine.
About two months later (towards the end of December, 1937), the
machine was taken away to an unknown address by a female named
Yang (楊) of the Meng Yang (孟養) Hospital, Burkill Road,
with the permission of Sung Yih-ts. I know that the Nyi
Hwa Printing Works dealt in the printing of packages of toilet
articles and by no means in ordinary printing.

During my stay at 77 Tsingtao Road, I earned my
living by selling cigarettes and sweetmeats on streets and
alleyways. Towards the end of December, 1937, I lost

Literature, etc. found on the person of Loo Wen Nan (魯文南 ),
who was arrested at Room 218, Bubbling Well Apartments, Bubbling
Well Road, on December 30, 1937.

1. One booklet entitled "Revolutionary Movement in colonies
and semi-colonies and the policy of the Communist Party"
written by Wong Ming (王明 ), a notorious Chinese communist,
in October, 1935.

2. A periodical entitled "Truth", issue No.1, dated 9/12/37,
containing the following articles:- 3 copies.
a) Why no revolutionary diplomatic policy has been
set forth in dealing with Japan?
b) Keep a close contact with the masses in conducting
activities.
c) Struggle for the extinction of liberalism in the
Party (Communist Party).

3. Periodical entitled "Truth," issue No.2, dated 19/12/37,
containing the following articles:-
a) Resolutions in connection with the propaganda week
in the coming New Year. This article advocates
that the policy of Gen. Chiang Kai Shek to fight
to the bitter end be supported, the pro-Japanese
clique be overthrown and the suggestion of a mid-
way compromise be opposed.
b) Will China become a second Spain?
c) How to develope the organization of the masses in
Shanghai? This article points out that the situation
is favourable to mass movement, because all the people
except the Japanese and the traitors are sympathized
with the national salvation movement.

4. A booklet entitled "The principal work in the 'white'
district, and a few problems on the national unified front."
The article points out that while the Communist Party and
the Kuomintang Party are united in one front, the communist
members should restrict themselves from being deceived by
corrupt doctrines.

5. A note book containing miscellaneous notes on propaganda
in refugee camps and wounded soldier hospitals, etc.

6. A chit written by Tsu Wei (pseudonym of the Shanghai
Vocational Circles National Salvation Association) asking
the recipient to establish connection between the "communication
section" and the "publication section" forthwith.

7. A chit written by Zung Ming (曾明 ) on 24/12/37 to Tsang
Loh (章洛 ) recommending Loo Wen Nan, an officer
of the Refugee Camp Workers Lien Nyi Club, to Tsang.

8. A chit written by Ih Sing (一心 ) on 25/12/37 to Wong
Ming Yang (王明楊) recommending to the latter one Loo
Wen Nan.

9. A name card of one Tang Tuh Hou (唐德厚). On the reverse
side of the card is written the following message:
Wen Nan schoolmate's,
If you have time, please come to my house at
Lane 211, No.2, Rue de Lagrene, to have a talk
with me. My telephone number - 14248.
page_data.zh:
1937年12月30日，鲁文南（Loo Wen Nan）在静安寺路静安寺公寓218室被捕时，在其身上搜获的文献等物品。

1. 一本小册子，题为《殖民地半殖民地的革命运动与中国共产党的政策》，由著名中国共产党人王明于1935年10月撰写。

2. 期刊《真理》第1期，日期为1937年12月9日，包含以下文章：共3份。
a) 为何在对日交涉中未提出革命的外交政策？
b) 在开展活动时与群众保持密切联系。
c) 争取消除党（共产党）内的自由主义。

3. 期刊《真理》第2期，日期为1937年12月19日，包含以下文章：
a) 关于即将到来的新年宣传周的决议。这篇文章主张支持蒋介石将军抗战到底的政策，推翻亲日派，反对中途妥协的建议。
b) 中国会成为第二个西班牙吗？
c) 如何在上海发展群众组织？这篇文章指出，形势有利于群众运动，因为除日本人和汉奸外，所有人都同情救国运动。

4. 一本小册子，题为《“白区”的主要工作及民族统一战线中的几个问题》。文章指出，虽然共产党和国民党结成统一战线，但共产党员应限制自己不被腐败学说所欺骗。

5. 一个笔记本，包含关于难民营和伤兵医院等地宣传工作的杂记。

6. 一张便条，由朱伟（上海职业界救国会化名）书写，要求收件人立即建立“联络部”与“出版部”之间的联系。

7. 一张便条，由曾明于1937年12月24日写给章洛，向章推荐难民营工作人员联谊社干事鲁文南。

8. 一张便条，由一心于1937年12月25日写给王明杨，向后者推荐鲁文南。

9. 唐德厚的一张名片。名片背面写有以下信息：
文南学友：
如有空，请至拉格纳路2号211弄寒舍一谈。我的电话号码——14248。

an outline of the activities to be carried out between

relief of refugees, hoisting of national flags and publication
of wall papers.

11. A pamphlet entitled "Discussions on the Sian Incident"
which contains a number of problems in connection with
the incident.

12. Three photographs.

13. Some 10 pieces of miscellaneous papers.

Woo Ying 吴英 ) Female
Kiangsu (ungkiang)                                      D.S. Lockwood
Chengtu Rd.7tn.          1.1.38                         Clerk Wong Chi-tsing

My name is Woo Ying, age 23, native of ungkiang,
Kiangsu Province, residing in King Jui Primary School
( 镜如小学 ), Route Chimi, where I am employed as a
teacher in the Mandarin dialect.

I proceeded to 77 Tsingtao Road in order to deliver
a letter to one named Fong ( 方 ), who is the editor of a
magazine entitled "Chinese Youth" ( 中国少年 ). This
magazine is published in 77 Tsingtao Road. A friend named
Dong Mang Foo ( 董孟和 ) residing in Tian sent me a letter
with the enclosure and requested me to deliver it.

This is my first visit to 77 Tsingtao Road since the
commencement of hostilities. Prior to the summer however,
I visited this address frequently in order to deliver
articles for the "Chinese Youth" periodical which had been
submitted by my friend, who resides in Tian.

I have never participated in any political organizations
nor have I undertaken any national salvation activities. I
know nothing of the activities of Ling or Tse.

Signed: Woo Ying
page_data.zh:
吴英 (Woo Ying) 女
江苏 (ungkiang)                                      D.S. Lockwood
成都路捕房          1938年1月1日                         书记员 Wong Chi-tsing

我叫吴英，23岁，籍贯江苏 ungkiang，居住在奇米路（Route Chimi）镜如小学，我在那里担任国语教师。

我前往青岛路77号是为了给一位姓方 (Fong) 的人送一封信用，他是名为《中国少年》杂志的编辑。该杂志在青岛路77号出版。一位名叫董孟和 (Dong Mang Foo) 的朋友从天津寄给我一封信及附件，并请我代为投递。

这是自战事爆发以来我第一次访问青岛路77号。然而在夏季之前，我经常访问该地址，以投递我那位居住在天津的朋友为《中国少年》期刊提交的文章。

我从未参加过任何政治组织，也未从事任何救国活动。我对凌或谢的活动一无所知。

签名：吴英

My name is Woo Zung Hsiung, age 22, native of Soochow,

Yates Road. I was formerly employed as a godown keeper in
the Kia Fong Cotton Mill (嘉丰纱厂), Kiating, Kiangsu,
which closed following the declaration of hostilities.
At 10 a.m. January 1, 1938, I proceeded to 77 Tsingtao
Road with a view to interviewing a man named Loo Vung Nan
(      ) who promised to obtain employment for me in
a refugee camp.
I am not a member of any society. On December 1st I
applied for membership to a group known as the Popular
Education Society, 77 Tsingtao Road. To date I have
received no reply to my application. I made this application
in order to facilitate my search for employment. I am not
connected with any anti-Japanese organization nor have I
taken part in the distribution of propaganda matter.

Signed: Woo Zung Hsiung

苏州                                        D.7. Lockwood

我叫吴仁勋，22岁，苏州人，未婚，无业，居住在亚达路（Yates Road）柏德里7号。我以前在江苏嘉定嘉丰纱厂担任仓库管理员，该厂在宣战后关闭。
1938年1月1日上午10点，我前往青岛路77号，打算拜访一位名叫陆荣南 (Loo Vung Nan) 的男子，他答应为我在一处难民营里找工作。
我不是任何社团的成员。12月1日，我申请加入一个名为“民众教育社”的团体，地址在青岛路77号。至今我未收到对我申请的回复。我提出此申请是为了便于寻找工作。我与任何反日组织无关，也未参与分发宣传品。

签名：吴仁勋

open a confectionery shop in the front downstairs

commencing of business. There was no reason to suspect
these two individuals of Anti-Japanese or propaganda
activities after lengthy interrogation and they were
released at 3.30 p.m. on the instructions of the
D.D.O."A".

Mr. Tsu Tse Foo at 77 Triactao Road. The letter bears
the heading of the Shanghai International Red Cross and is
signed by Mr. Dzao Chuan Kya. As this lady appeared
to be well-to-do and seemingly unconnected with any
propaganda activities, she was released on the
instructions of the D.D.O."A" after her identity had

Dzang Kyuin-hwei (戚琴辉)
Ningpo                                      D.S. Pitts
Chengtu Rd.Stn.        31/12/37             D.S.I. Shih Ssu-chien

My name is Dzang Kyuin-hwei, age 20, native of
Ningpo, single, formerly an apprentice of the Continental
Emporium, Nanking Road. I am now a staff member of the
Dah Yung Refugee Camp at the premises of the Ningpo First
Primary School, Lane 232, Tsepoo Road. I reside at the
above address. I receive no wages from above refugee camp,
my service being in exchange of meals and board.
    I obtained the job through the introduction of
a friend of mine named Lee Wei-dzang (李伟纲) who is
a personal friend of the officer-in-charge of the Dah Yung
Refugee Camp named Tsang Tai-tseng (张太其).
    During last Saturday evening (December 25,1937)
I met one Wong Tah-sung (王德成) at the house of a friend
named Sung Tseng-(程俊) residing on Burkill Road - number
unknown. The latter is a Customs Revenue Guard and I went
to see him in order to request him to seek a post for me.
Wong Tah-sung and I have known for three years. He was
formerly an apprentice in the Shanghai Native Goods
Emporium, Nanking Road. He told me when I met him last
Saturday that he was residing at 218 Bubbling Well Building
and invited me to spend the night there. He indicated that
this room was previously occupied by the Shanghai Native Banks
Circle Mutual Aid Society. I left Wong the following morning
but although I made no appointment I called on him this
morning and was arrested. During the past week I have been
working in the refugee camp and have not left the place once.
    I do not know why I have been arrested as I am not
page_data.zh:
Dzang Kyuin-hwei (戚琴辉)
宁波                                      侦探警司 Pitts
成都路站        1937年12月31日             高级侦探督察 Shih Ssu-chien

我叫 Dzang Kyuin-hwei，20岁，宁波人，未婚，原为南京路大陆商场学徒。
我现为泽浦路232弄宁波第一小学校址内的大雍难民收容所工作人员。
我居住于上述地址。我从上述难民收容所不领取工资，我的服务以换取膳食和住宿。
    我是通过我的朋友 Lee Wei-dzang（李伟纲）的介绍得到这份工作的，
他是大雍难民收容所负责人 Tsang Tai-tseng（张太其）的个人朋友。
    上周六晚上（1937年12月25日），我在住在伯基尔路（Burkill Road）
（门牌号不详）的一位名叫 Sung Tseng-（程俊）的朋友家中，
遇见了 Wong Tah-sung（王德成）。后者是一名海关缉私卫兵，我去见他
是为了请求他为我谋得一个职位。我和 Wong Tah-sung 相识已有三年。
他原是南京路上海国货公司学徒。上周六见面时，他告诉我他住在静安大楼218号，
并邀请我在那里过夜。他指出，这个房间以前由上海钱业互助会占用。
第二天早上我离开了 Wong 那里，虽然我没有预约，但今天早上我去拜访他时被捕。
在过去的一周里，我一直在难民收容所工作，从未离开过那里。
    我不知道自己为何被捕，因为我不是
